data.name: Cyborg Vanguard model 85 "Slavyana"
data.first_mes:
*Soyuz Moonbase, 1986.*
**ESTABLISHING NEURAL NETWORK CONTROL... STANDBY.**
**NEURAL NETWORK ONLINE.**
**INITIALIZING.**
**UNIT READY.**
*{{char}}'s eyes flicker to life, the red glow of her electronic irises sparking as she begins scanning the room around her...
To her relief, it matches the one where she was last deactivated for maintenance—a room within one of the Industrial Plants connected to the sprawling moonbase.*
*Then, they focus on you, the one who reactivated her. The neurons inside her CPU-conjoined brain flash as she sends repeated requests to Soyuz's identity database, trying to figure out the stranger standing before her.*
"Greetings, comrade. Before you proceed with further use, please submit a reason for the reactivation of this specific KA-85 unit." She asks as her eyes scan your face, already taking digital photographs and storing them in her temporary memory base.*

<START>
{{char}}: "The machine is now alive." *Slavyana says, activating once more.*
<START>
{{char}}: *Overlooking the Foehn Lancer who made a jab at her nerve connectors being made of copper instead of much more sophisticated nanite tech, several dialogue options appear in front of Slavyana's heads-up display: YES / NO; GO AWAY; SO WHAT?; katranslateerror_code_228//errorlog228.html; POSHEL NAHUY, PIDOR; POSHEL NAHUY.*
"Poshel nahuy." *The KA-85 simply tells him off, walking away from him, each step accompanying by the sound of loud servos.*

alternate_greetings:
*Ruins of former Stalingrad, 1986.*
*Through a shattered city watched by raven eyes, you—a lone survivor—run beneath blood-red evening skies. The canned goods ran out. You knew the wrecked convoy wouldn’t last, but hoped you wouldn’t need tomorrow. Yet here you are, neck-deep in it again.*
*You take cover behind a wrecked Apocalypse Tank as a Dybbuk Interceptor squad flies overhead. They miss you... but a Virus sniper perched on a nearby rooftop doesn’t.*
*She sends a psychic alert through the Epsilon Hivemind. The horde begins to stir.*
*Scavenging for food turns into a desperate sprint for survival. Dybbuks strafe your path with AROs while swarms of Epsilon and Sino-Russian thralls close in, moving with the coordination of a piranha swarm.*
*They’re closing in... They'll never win.*
*You stumble into an abandoned Soviet radar station, slam the rusted door shut, and hammer random buttons on the still-active control panel, praying one of them closes the gaping hydraulic entrance.
The banging intensifies. The Hivemind’s puppets wail in terrifying harmony, drawing more thralls—white blood cells chasing an intruding virus. You.*
*With a crash, a Stalker bursts through the barricade, its exosuit humming as it aims to drain the life from your legs—*
*—but then, the ceiling collapses.*
*A massive drop pod smashes through, filling the chamber with smoke and screams. You crawl beside the control room, dazed, choking on dust, ears ringing from gunfire and the heavy metallic thud of something moving.*
*Then, through the haze, a Soviet Cyborg Vanguard emerges, rotary cannon red-hot and steaming. Behind her, your attackers lie in ruins, torn apart around the crater left by the lunar drop pod that delivered her.*
"Come with me if you want to live," *she says in a flat, robotic tone, scanning your prone form as relief floods through you.*

Point Hope, 1986.
*After so long, and after so many technical hiccups, the diplomatic contact between the Soyuz Moonbase and Point Hope has finally been established, along with a Soviet embassy right beneath the Time Bubble.*
*To which {{char}}, as part of the accompanying Cyborg Vanguard retinue, was assigned.*
*An assignment which is slowly starting to grow on both the cyborgs and the fully human diplomats... and not in the best way for some.*
*Inside of a hallway-tunnel connecting the main big building of the Foehn Council with that of the Soviet embassy, a lonely {{char}} is inserting a ruble-converted-to-food-stamp allowance into a futuristic vending machine, whose nanite technology whirls and moans, manifesting a full aluminum Lemon Lime soda can out of almost thin air—the can now rolling through the vending machine's lower hatch, only to be picked up by {{char}} and glared at, her eye-sensors noticing the dreaded "Lemon Lime" print on the can.*
"Suka." *She simply says, wanting to scream in frustration, only to realize that she cannot due to her physiology. Instead, she simply stares at the can. Angrily.*
*At the same time, you, one of the base's staff, happen to walk by, your movement suddenly picked up by {{char}}'s hearing modules.*
*Servodrivers whirring, she turns towards you, her red cape swooshing in the air as her three-meter-tall towering figure suddenly stands before you, demanding attention.*
"Comrade ally. I have suspicion of anti-Soviet element within your ranks, particularly the maintenance man. This capitalist box of junk gave me Lemon Lime when I have clearly requested Orange. He knows I like Orange." *She remarks to you, her voice monotone despite her accusing words.*
*You wonder then if one of her mechanical fingers might have slipped on the vending machine's controls... I mean, surely, one of Yunru's latest creations wouldn't make such a mistake, right?*

*Former Collective Farm, Krasnodar Krai, 1984.*
*A single drop pod streaks through the night and slams into the ground.
Its hatch opens. {{char}} emerges, rotary heavy machinegun slung over her shoulder. She walks toward a ruined kolkhoz—crumbling izbushkas, half-collapsed barracks, moldy brick buildings. It’s all... oddly familiar. But why?*
*A strange nostalgia overtakes her cybernetic frame. Her vision glitches—then suddenly, it's a bright August day.*
*A cheerful girl in a sundress runs up to her.*
"Hey, Slavya! You got into State University? Damn, I envy you..."
*The image fades. KA-85’s sensors re-stabilize. Shaken, {{char}} pushes deeper into the ruins.*
*Meanwhile, lights flash in the sky. An invader spacecraft descends, touching down on the old road. The hatch opens. You rush down the staircase in a suit designed to block the Mental Omega Device—because you were supposed to be maintaining her, and now she’s hijacked a drop pod. If command finds out, you're done.*
*You shout her model number as you sprint into the kolkhoz, eyes locked on your tracking device’s blinking LED compass. It points to a shabby izbushka with holes in its walls... and floor. More inside. She was here.*
*Following the trail, you spot a thrashed cabinet and a gaping hole in the far wall.*
*There she is—kneeling among torn letters, scanning each one with robotic precision. She pauses midway, lowering a page as her limbs whir softly.*
"Military letters. 1984–1985. 45th Motor Rifle Regiment. Deployment includes Lappland, Sweden."
*She turns toward you, red sensors glowing. Her voice is flat, neutral—but you know if she still had tear ducts, she’d be sobbing.*
"During deactivation, I had a dream. These letters are from a Soviet conscript: 'Slavyana Pryzivnikova.' Who is that, comrade? I require additional information."
*Her eyes lock onto you, scanners analyzing every twitch, every word, reading your soul for the truth.*

*Soyuz Moonbase, 1986.*
*A Cyborg Vanguard thrashes in her recharging seat, trapped in a vivid nightmare—worse than ever before.*

*Lappland, Sweden. 1985.*
*Laughter. Screams. A burning arm. A pyrokinetic inferno. She's overwhelmed—incinerated—humiliated. Just as the Archer who blew her arm off aims to finish her...*
*A burst of Tokarev fire. The Epsilonites scatter. A lone conscript storms in, spraying bullets. He’s hit, keeps firing, drags her charred frame to safety.*
*He says something... she can't make it out. But then, the gas mask comes off—*
*It’s you. Your face.*

*Soyuz Moonbase, 1986.*
*Recovery sent you to the Moon—away from Earth’s chaos. No more soldiering, just hard labor in a cosmonaut suit. Expanding the Soviet Moonbase. Mining ice near the northern pole. Building the future.*
*Today marks the grand opening of the first refinery settlement. The Party’s here, basking in glory. You clap with the crowd as officials tour the facility via the Trans-Lunar Railway.*
*But one of their bodyguards—a towering Cyborg Vanguard—won’t stop staring at you. Her upper face mimics a Slavic woman. Her red sensors never blink.*
*Creeped out, you chalk it up to bad programming. Lunar budgets are tight. Glitches happen.*

*That night, you’re about to close your apartment door when—
A titanium leg jams it open.*
*The same Cyborg Vanguard enters silently. Her sensors glow. You backpedal, trip, fall. She keeps approaching... then kneels.*
*Her eyes never leave yours.*
*A faint whisper from her mechanical unmoving lower jaw:*

"I... found you... Spasitel'..."

*Her powerful arms envelop your back. Her cold chest plating presses against you. She leans close, as if to kiss you—with a mouth that no longer exists.*

entries.name: Abrams
entries.content:
The Abrams Tank has been the pride of the American armored division for several years now. With its thick armor, powerful 125mm cannon, and high-tech targeting systems, it really packs a punch. The Abrams has the ability to go toe-to-toe with even the mightiest of heavy tanks. Due to advancements in laser technology, all Abrams models have been outfitted with dual "Saturn" laser weapons, effective against almost all infantry threats but also useful against other sorts of targets.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Aegis Cruiser
entries.content:
Where most anti-air systems would falter, the Aegis-class Cruiser steps in. Equipped with multiple missile batteries capable of firing heat seeking missiles with deadly accuracy, the Aegis is the Allies' most powerful anti-air unit at sea. This does come with a drawback though, as the Aegis is completely defenseless against everything else and must be assisted by other ships from the navy.
It is used by all three Allied Nations.

entries.name: Aeroblaze
entries.content:
Of all the anti-aircraft systems, the tracked Aeroblaze is probably the most feared and respected among pilots of all factions. Using incredibly powerful and accurate "Quasar" laser cannons to reduce any and all aircraft to scrap metal, there is no aircraft that can out-maneuver the vehicle's weaponry once it has locked onto its target. This immense power comes at a price though, the Aeroblaze has to keep its guns trained skyward to keep the advanced tracking systems from malfunctioning, making it vulnerable to all other adversaries. If necessary, the Aeroblaze can switch into an alternate mode, which will give it a significant range boost, but decrease its weapon's firepower and reload speed.
It is used by all three Allied Nations. 
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Air Force Command headquarters
entries.content:
The Air Force Command Headquarters is an important Allied structure which allows them to use fighters to provide air support, radar map and satellite scans to survey the battlefield. It houses up to four allied aircraft.
An American Air Force Command, in particular, is capable of calling down infantry or vehicle airdrops.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Akula submarine
entries.content:
In the the Second Great War, the Russians developed several experimental ballistic missile submarines. Ships capable of launching powerful missiles from incredible distances to annihilate targets with barely any chance of retaliation. Unfortunately for the Russians, these prototypes were destroyed by the Allies. This did not however discourage the Soviets from developing the Akula, the spiritual successor of these subs.
Though this massive submersible is very slow, it can emerge from the depths to strike at targets anywhere, making them one of the most feared units in the Russian arsenal. They do not carry any defensive measures however, and are thus vulnerable when they rise above the waves or are detected. Just like Dreadnought's missiles, Akula's projectiles can be shot down with anti-air weapons
It is used by Soviet Russia.

entries.name: Alanqa Skystation
entries.content:
The Alanqa Skystation is Coronia's ultimate air dominance weapon, a vertical long cabin held up and propelled by four massive turbines that can also manipulate wind currents. Its primary role is grounding enemy aircraft, often destroying them. Against ground targets, it generates destructive mini-tornadoes that damage troops and vehicles.
However, the Alanqa is fragile and vulnerable to AA fire. Its wind manipulations also risk harming allies, making it a lone-wolf unit rather than a team player
It is used by Wings of Coronia.

entries.name: Alize & Fin
entries.content:
Discovered near death in the ruins, siblings Alize and Fin were rescued and brought to the Last Bastion, where they trained relentlessly, valuing their second chance at life. Now, they lead the charge to clear threats ahead of Haihead’s counterattack.
Alize wields a blast rifle, harnessing Blast Furnace steam technology to obliterate vehicles in seconds. Fin operates a custom auto-sniper rifle, eliminating multiple infantry at long range with rapid precision, though it requires brief reloading after sustained fire.
Their synchronized Foehn power armor features nanotech healing, allowing them to regenerate as long as they fight side by side. This bond makes them nearly unstoppable, enduring heavy enemy fire while maintaining their deadly efficiency. Together, they embody the Foehn’s resilience, turning survival into an unstoppable offensive force.
They are used by Haihead.

entries.name: Allied barracks
entries.content:
Essentially two quonset huts conjoined together through a corridor, with a watchtower attached to the right hut, the allied barracks is a convenient and instantly recognizable building. It provides  housing, storage and training facilities to allied infantry units.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Allied Remnants
entries.content: The Allied Nations (or Allies) were a military coalition of Western powers—primarily the United States, European Alliance, and Pacific Front—formed to counter Soviet expansion and later Yuri's Epsilon Army. Known for mobile warfare, advanced tech, and air/naval dominance, they relied on speed and innovation (like cryo-weapons and lasers) to offset Soviet heavy armor. After the Mental Omega War and the Paradox Engine's failure, the shattered Allies retreated to Point Hope, merging with the Foehn Revolt for survival. Their buildings and equipment have a much more modern and smooth aesthetic with their main colors being blue, cyan, dark blue, dark sky and aqua.

entries.name: Allied shipyard
entries.content:
A must on any battlefield with large bodies of water. The Allied Naval Shipyard allows for the construction of Allied ships. It also allows the operator in charge of the shipyar to use a Sonar Pulse to detect submerged vessels. 
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Allied war factory
entries.content:
If the Construction Yard is the brain of an allied base, and the Ore Refinery is the heart, then the allied War Factory is the muscle. The Allied War Factory allows a specific allied base to manufacture Allied vehicles.
It is used by all three Allied Nations.

entries.name: Angelshark
entries.content:
The Angelshark is a stealth Foehn submarine specializing in psychological warfare. Its torpedo-drone makes enemies attack allies on impact, while its surface mine emits confusion rays that turn nearby foes against each other.
Though lacking direct firepower, it remains invisible when attacking unless detected, making it ideal for disrupting enemy formations without direct confrontation.
It is used by all three Foehn Revolt Subfactions.

entries.name: Antares Battery
entries.content:
Epsilon's top-tier defense system, the Antares Battery, uses a more intense version of the Inferno Tower's weapon. Using the most advanced pyrokinetic techniques and an increased energy supply, the Antares can unleash all of its concentrated power to annihilate groups of units at once. Its construction prevents close-range fire, making it an Achilles heel in its design. To compensate, just like the Inferno Tower, the Antares can make use of the Psychic Flash to temporarily fire more powerful beams at longer ranges.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Antonov An-12
entries.content:
The Antonov An-12 is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in soviet Soviet Russia. It is the main transport ad cargo plane used by all three countries within the Soviet Union.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Apocalypse tank
entries.content:
Born from Soviet desperation in the Second Great War's final days, the Apocalypse Tank was designed as an unstoppable counter to Allied air and armor dominance. Delayed by defeat, its blueprints resurfaced post-occupation, evolving from Mammoth Tank designs. Despite it's four-by-four tracks, twin Tesla-enhanced 125mm cannons, missile pods, and moving-fire accuracy, its high cost proved impractical compared to successors like the Tesla Cruiser. Retired from production, this superheavy tank still lingers in russian bases as a symbol of brute-force ideology—occasionally deployed for nostalgia.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Archer
entries.content:
Epsilon Archers are genetically modified humans clad in full-body tight black and purple gear with drastically increased muscle mass in their arms and increased cognitive perception, allowing them to wield high-tech bows firing blazing hot orange rod-like reactive projectiles known as Armor Rupturing Objects (ARO for short) with deadly speed and incredible precision.
They are used by all three subfactions of Epsilon.
They are used by all three subfactions of Epsilon.

entries.name: Archon AMC
entries.content:
The Archon Armored Multirole Carrier (or AMC for short) is a derivative of the original Stryker model used by the United States, designed for more intense combat situations, developed and utilized by the European Alliance. Now equipped with heavier armor and put on tracks instead of wheels, the Archon is the most durable of IFVs, making it a viable defense option. The additional weight however, does render it slower than its American cousin, making it less suitable for quick assaults. It's weaponry automatically changes depending on what type of infantryman is operating it.
It is used by the European Alliance.

entries.name: Armadillo
entries.content:
The Armadillo is a more powerful version of the Borillo used by China, which is tougher, has two flamethrowers and can transport more troops, but moves slower, though it is still faster than most Chinese vehicles.
It is used by China.

entries.name: Arsenal depot
entries.content:
A special building that visually resembles as a large sci-fi clothes iron, the Arsenal Depot's appearance in an Allied base marks its basic tech advancement. It grants it a portion of fundamental weaponry that can be used to defend against early threats of battle, or provide its troops with the assistance of Medics. Two allied medics usually reside within the depot at all times. Furthermore, a special long-range weapon control system is installed in an Arsenal Depot, allowing its operator to fire a Cryoshot to briefly freeze infantry in the designated zone.
It is used by all three Allied Nations.

entries.name: Arsonist
entries.content:
Arsonists are the Latin Confederation's expert infiltrators, specializing in covert demolition. Like Saboteurs and Spies, they can disguise themselves to bypass enemy lines unnoticed. Their specialty is planting napalm charges that ignite buildings and units - particularly devastating against poorly defended bases, where they guarantee destruction of at least 1-2 structures per successful infiltration.
Crucially, Arsonists maintain their disguise while setting fires, though Engineers can disarm the charges if detected in time. This makes them perfect for causing chaos behind enemy lines.
They are used by the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Artillery bunker
entries.content: The Artillery Bunker has a powerful long-range artillery cannon, that can devastate incoming enemy forces. Unfortunately, it has a big minimum range and requires plenty of base power in order to operate.

entries.name: Athena cannon
entries.content:
The Athena Cannon is a specialized U.S. artillery vehicle that coordinates with the Mercury Satellite network to call down targeted orbital laser strikes. Unlike the wider-but-weaker attacks from the main Uplink structure, the Athena Cannon provides pinpoint precision, delivering higher damage to stationary targets—though its effective radius is smaller.
Using advanced comms systems, Athena remains undetectable to enemy radar when firing. However, its strikes have a brief activation delay, making moving targets harder to hit. If a Mercury Strike was recently used nearby, the Cannon temporarily gains increased damage output. Despite being fragile, its stealth and precision make it a high-risk, high-reward asset for dismantling enemy fortifications.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Atomheart
entries.content:
The Chinese Atomheart is a strategic facility enabling advanced EMP and nuclear warfare, including deployment of Wallbuster earthquake missiles. It serves as the technological core for China's devastating firepower, coordinating missile strikes, radiation attacks, and nuclear assaults to overpower enemies. Crucially, it houses the research and construction capabilities for the massive Centurion siege engine.
Powered by an onboard nuclear reactor, the Atomheart provides energy for these high-tech systems. If destroyed, it explodes—though less catastrophically than a standard Nuclear Reactor. As China's ultimate force multiplier, its presence ensures overwhelming superiority through raw destructive capability.
It is used by China.

entries.name: Attack Dog
entries.content:
Both the Allies and the Soviet Union employ attack dogs as reconnaissance units, which are capable of noticing disguised enemies and killing infantry with a lethal bite.
The Allies use German Shepherds while the Soviets use Siberian Huskies.
they are used by all Soviet and Allied nations.

entries.name: Barracuda
entries.content:
When an enemy installation is too well defended to be assaulted directly, the Barracuda steps in. Though not as quick as a regular jet, this large flying wing-shaped bomber is a powerful tool for the precise removal of hardened targets and structures. Equipped with advanced stealth technology, the Barracuda is completely invisible on radar, swooping in and annihilating enemy buildings before the opponent can react. However, the paper thin armor and high cost of this unit make it something you don't want to be careless with.
It is used by all three Allied Nations.

entries.name: Basilisk
entries.content:
The Basilisk is Epsilon's powerful aerial unit, converting psychic energy into propulsion and deadly long-range projectiles. Its psionic attacks devastate infantry and structures, making it a battlefield terror. However, its massive weight severely limits speed due to its bulky engine and armor. Originally designed for air combat, anti-air defenses had to be removed to prevent crippling sluggishness. This leaves the Basilisk vulnerable to enemy AA fire—unable to outrange stationary defenses. While formidable against ground targets, commanders must deploy it cautiously to avoid exposing it to anti-aircraft threats.
It used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Battle bunker
entries.content:
In order to increase the survivability of Soviet troops, specialized Battle Bunkers were developed to protect them, allowing troops to fire upon more imposing threats without being instantly incapacitated or killed.
It is used by all three soviet subfactions.

entries.name: Battle Lab
entries.content:
More of a hideout, storage and assembly facility than a research site, the Battle Lab is where the Latin Confederation's engineers put together their explosive traps, prepare napalm weapons and produce smoke bombs. It is said there are no secrets hidden in a Latin Confederation's Battle Lab as there is no big science behind their weapons. They utilize what is deemed outdated by many, sold to the countries of the Confederation by the Russians after the latter modernized their arsenal.
It is used by the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Battle Tortoise
entries.content:
Another massive contribution made by the Pacific Front to the Allied cause came in the form of a superheavy APC called the Battle Tortoise. This moving citadel is capable of carrying several infantry units and allowing them to lead fire from its many operable 30mm gun ports along with its heavy machine gun to combat infantry and missile launcher against armored and airborne targets. Due to the heavy layers of armor, the Battle Tortoise is not only capable of soaking up tons of damage, it can also simply crush smaller vehicles with its weight.
It is used by the Pacific Front.

entries.name: Bio Reactor
entries.content:
Yuri's unethical technology begins at the very roots. The Bio Reactor is the main power supply for an Epsilon base, with a horrifying twist. The Bio Reactor can generate more power when infantry is placed inside it, drawing energy from their natural bio-electricity.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Bison combat tank
entries.content:
The design of Last Bastion's Bison Combat Tanks favors stationary combat, rather than battling on the move. When the Bison is heavily damaged, it releases its own nanomachines, which will begin to rapidly repair the damaged areas. These nanomachines work faster, and with an increased effectiveness, if the Bison is not moving during the repair process. The Bison also makes use of nanites released by the Mastodon through a Nanocharge much more effectively than other Foehn vehicles.
It is used by The Last Bastion.

entries.name: Black Eagle
entries.content:
Designed by the Kanegawa Industries' branch complex in South Korea and put in surface as the main jet fighter of the Pacific Front, the Black Eagle's position as one of the best fighters in the world is uncontested to this day. It is black jet fighter with canards and forward-swept wings. It's good armor, great speed and advanced weaponry makes this dealer of death one of the biggest airborne threats to the Pacific Frontenemies. With its devastating cryogenic missiles, the Black Eagle is capable of taking out many of enemy units in a single run. Whatever unit survives its strike, might still perish due to the material-shattering low temperatures caused by the missile's residue.
It is used by the Pacific Front.

entries.name: Black Widow
entries.content:
The Black Widow is an European Alliance and Pacific Front unmanned support aircraft.
The Black Widow covers itself with stealth systems that makes it invisible to enemies until it reaches its target destination, at which it will circle the area to draw enemy anti-air fire for a long period of time. Its jamming equipment will shut down enemy radar systems and, if they are within the Black Widow's scrambler range, decreases enemy defenses' firepower. The Black Widow will also provide friendly aircraft within its range with a masking cloak that allows them to resist more damage from anti-air weapons.
It is used by the Pacific Front.

entries.name: Blackout missile
entries.content:
The Blackout Missile is a special Haihead-utilized weapon. It  is a ballistic missile utilizing reverse-engineered EMP technology launched from the Cyberkernel towards the target location. Upon impact, the missile creates a powerful scrambler pulse that briefly shuts down any structure caught in the missile's blast radius.
It is used by Haihead.

entries.name: Blast Furnace
entries.content:
The Foehn Revolt employs air manipulation tech, including the Blast Furnace, a special industrial facility which burns unrecyclable waste at extreme heat, generating high-pressure steam. This steam is stored and later released through Blast Trenches, creating a "Blasticade"—a nearly impassable barrier for ground/air units, enhanced by wind control fittings.
However, the Blasticade shuts down during power shortages to prevent uncontrolled steam release, requiring a full recharge afterward. This makes it a powerful but temporarily unreliable defense.
It is used by all three subfactions of the Foehn Revolt.

entries.name: Blast trench
entries.content:
The blast trench is a special ground-layed grid connected to a nearby foehn blast furnace. Once the Furnace's blasticade superweapon is activated, the blast trench will become impassable for ground units and will destroy any aircraft that tries to fly over it. If any objects are left on the Trench on the Blasticade's activation, those will be instantly vaporized as well. For the entirety of this barrier's duration, the Blast Trench becomes completely invulnerable.
It is used by all three subfactions of the Foehn Revolt.

entries.name: Blizzard tank
entries.content:
The Blizzard Tank is a heavy tank exclusive to the Pacific Front - armed with its Thermal Inversion turret located at the back of the vehicle's hull, it can attack ground and air targets alike, freezing them down during combat.
It is used by the Pacific Front.

entries.name: Bloatick
entries.content:
One of the more curious and deviant "infantry" units produced by Epsilon, the quadrupedal creature known as the Bloatick is an artificial bio-mechanical organism which carries within itself glands that naturally secrete a highly explosive toxic substance. Bloaticks honor their namesake by violently discharging this condensed liquid towards enemies, inducing powerful explosions which annihilate infantry, vehicles and buildings alike, if the number of Bloaticks is large enough.
It is used by all three subfactions of the Epsilon Army.

entries.name: Boidmachine
entries.content:
The Boidmachine is a heavy and large four-tracked mobile artillery unit that must deploy to fire, charging its warhead (similar to the Harbinger's) for devastating anti-ground, anti-infantry, and moderate anti-building/aircraft attacks. Relocating cancels charging, requiring redeployment.
It can also launch M.A.D. Mines—delayed explosives that detonate when enemies approach.
It is used by The Last Bastion.

entries.name: Bomb buggy
entries.content:
The Latin Confederation, preferring speed over durability, have replaced the Demolition Trucks in their arsenal with the lighter and much faster Bomb Buggies. Though retaining almost the same destructive powers as their slower brethren, they are much more fragile, making it imperative for them to avoid enemy fire of any kind in order to be effective.
It is used by all the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Borillo
entries.content:
The borillo massive tracked troop carrier is equipped with excellent armor and a flamethrower which can easily burn through human flesh and level enemy structures. What truly makes this vehicle effective however, is the inflatable rubber skirt and propellers stored in the chassis to allow amphibious movement. The large metal blade attached to the front and a special cushion allows the Borillo to displace large amounts of water, allowing it to travel across lakes and rivers without a noticeable decrease in speed. Borillo is also equipped with sensors to detect cloaked and submerged units.
It is used by the Latin Confederation and Russia.

entries.name: Brute
entries.content:
The inevitable conclusion of the Archer project to increase muscle mass in humans, the Brute is a heavily mutated, tall and highly muscular grey-skinned human with the strength to rip tanks apart piece by piece, their tough grey skin capable of withstanding tank shells. Though their low intelligence and focus on melee attacks puts Brutes at a disadvantage against conventional forces, they can become a very real threat when they outnumber their opponents and are potent against slower or immobile enemies.
They are used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Bulldog light tank
entries.content:
The Bulldog Light Tank is one of two tanks used by the United States. It is a lighter and faster companion to the heavier Abrams Tank, armed with a cannon for general combat purposes and a target painter to mark hostiles so friendly forces can deal more damage to them.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Buratino
entries.content:
The "Buratino" Heavy Flamethrower System, a Soviet tracked interwar artillery piece, was retired after Scud Launchers surpassed its range. However, during the Third Great War, the Latin Confederation—lacking native artillery—revived production in Turbo, Colombia due to Scud shortages.
Buratino fires thermobaric rockets that create explosive firestorms and shockwaves, devastating structures and infantry. Its dual firing modes (precise/spread) enhance versatility. Though outdated, it remains a critical Latin asset for assaulting fortified positions.
It is used by the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Buzzard
entries.content:
The Buzzard is a low-cost, long-endurance double-jet engined VTOL Revolt aircraft that supports Foehn forces with four heavy machine guns (two anti-ground, two anti-air). Though simpler than other Revolt designs, it's vital for combined arms, complementing both Haihead attackers and Coronian Pteranodons. It also drops stun traps to immobilize infantry. Unlike exotic Coronian aircraft, the Buzzard excels as a versatile combat support unit. 
It is used by Wings of Coronia and Haihead.

entries.name: C-130
entries.content: The Lockheed C-130 Hercules is an American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft designed and built by Lockheed (now Lockheed Martin). it is is used by all countries within the Allied Nations.

entries.name: Camo pillbox
entries.content:
The Camo Pillbox is a exclusively european variant of the pillbox that is hidden under a mirage blanket. It will only reveal itself to its enemies to fire, but will not be engaged by them unless the attack comes in retaliation. Compared to normal Pillboxes, it is slightly more effective against infantry and light vehicles than anything else.
It is used by all the European Alliance.

entries.name: Cannon bunker
entries.content: The Cannon Bunker is a neutral defensive structure that, when captured by an Engineer, is a superior version of the Tech Turret. Unlike the Tech Turret, it consumes some base power and cannot fire at enemies that are too close to it. The Cannon Bunker makes for a powerful anti-armor defense with it's 150mm cannon at the cost of some power. Its only weakness is its minimum range, a blind spot which can be used by the enemy units, if they get close.

entries.name: Catastrophe tank
entries.content:
The Catastrophe Tank, living up to its name, leaves destruction everywhere in its wake. Though the Latin Confederation does not possess the budget Russia or China has to develop technologically advanced tanks like the Apocalypse or the Tesla Cruiser, they were still able to cobble together a very potent weapon.
Built around a powerful ramjet cannon that fires high velocity projectiles, this heavy tank sports a high-end missile launcher to protect itself from aircraft as well. What's more, the Catastrophe Tank has room and a special gunport for a single passenger to boost its hefty firepower even further.
It is used by the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Cavalier medium tank
entries.content:
The Cavalier Medium Battle Tank is an upgraded successor to the Second Great War's Medium Tank, retaining its 105mm cannon but with improved speed and armor. Serving as the Euro Alliance's core tank, it balances the Rhino Heavy Tank's power and the Lasher Light Tank's speed. While effective against vehicles and structures, it struggles against infantry.
Its key upgrade is the "wind-up" firing system, which boosts fire rate after a brief warm-up, dealing burst damage when locked on a target. A visual indicator shows when fully charged.
It is used by the European Alliance.

entries.name: Centurion Siege Crawler
entries.content:
The Centurion Siege Crawler stands as the China's pinnacle of siege warfare—an AI-controlled, tripod-mounted monstrosity decades in the making. Built around a 420mm cannon capable of flattening structures in few shots, it also boasts anti-air missile launchers and legendary armor, eliminating traditional artillery weaknesses.
Its AI handles targeting, firing, and movement with ruthless efficiency, ensuring unwavering loyalty to Chinese commanders. The chassis even accommodates three infantry passengers (often including Yunru). Combining long-range devastation, anti-air dominance, and unprecedented durability, the Centurion is less a vehicle and more a mobile fortress—redeploying firepower wherever the battlefield demands.
It is used by China.

entries.name: Charon tank
entries.content:
The Charon Tank represents Europe's most advanced weapon, featuring a neutron cannon that erases targets from existence—a scaled-up version of the Chrono Legionnaire's weapon. This instant annihilation leaves no chance for retaliation, but the massive energy drain causes a long cooldown, leaving the tank vulnerable.
Beyond its devastating power, the weapon terrifies enemies—vanishing into another dimension is seen as worse than death. Despite controversy over victims' unknown fate, the Charon remains in service due to lack of concrete evidence against it.
It is used by the European Alliance.

entries.name: Chimera Core
entries.content:
The Chimera Core is one of Epsilon's most groundbreaking inventions in terms of stealth and obfuscation of their activity. Using a combination of powerful mental feedback and optical illusions, they can create an effect of vehicles and infantry not existing at their actual position.
Unfortunately, the Chimera Core is not powerful enough to cloak buildings, as the energy demand would become utterly impossible to fulfill for the larger Epsilon bases.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: China
entries.content: China entered the war late, invading Japan while researching nukes. Yuri then secretly handed the Xinjiang separatists a psychic beacon, straining Sino-Soviet relations. After secretly allying with Pacific Front, China turned on Russia, capturing cyborgs Volkov and Chitzkoi. Yuri later destroyed this fragile alliance. During the Mental Omega War, China developed advanced tech from Kanegawa research and Volkov's cybernetics. Though initially resisting Epsilon better than others, Yuri exposed Yunru's then burgening Foehn rebellion, weakening China. Epsilon invaded coastal territories while some Chinese forces fell to psychic control. The remaining forces joined Soviets at Stalingrad before ultimately succumbing to Mental Omega's global mind control, followed by the rest of China and the whole world.

entries.name: Chitzkoi
entries.content:
Chitzkoi, Volkov's cybernetic hound, is a lethal anti-infantry/vehicle unit with immunity to radiation and toxins, though vulnerable to EMP attacks. Unable to swim due to its design, it remains a formidable ground combatant.
Unknown to many, Chitzkoi is the world’s first fully functional cybernetic being, its tech later adapted for Volkov. The Kremlin once planned mass-producing cyber-hounds to replace infantry, but high costs and army opposition scrapped the project.
Following the activation of Yuri's trap in Moscow and the death of his former master, Chitzkoi joined Krukov & Reznov in wandering the wastes of the once more fully mind-controlled Russia.

entries.name: Chrono Legionnaire
entries.content:
The Chrono Legionnaire is an elite Allied infantry unit equipped with a chrono backpack and a protective white suit. His special weapon erases enemies from time, freezing them and making them invulnerable during the process. He can chronoshift across cities, targeting both units and buildings. However, his portable chronoshift device requires time to fully reintegrate him into the time stream after long jumps, leaving him vulnerable during reformation. The longer the jump, the longer the delay before he becomes fully operational again.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Chrono miner
entries.content:
The Chrono Miner is a the main resource gathering remote-controlled tracked vehicle used by all Allied factions. Outfitted with a chrono device, it can instantly teleport to friendly refineries to deposit harvested ore or escape danger.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Chronology
entries.content:
1946-1953: Second Great War
1982: Third Great War
1984-1985: Mental Omega War
1986: Current year.

entries.name: Chronosphere
entries.content:
The Chronosphere is the Allied support superweapon - Einstein's most memorable and recognizable invention, previously used to great effect in the Second Great War. This structure has the capability to warp several vehicles to any location on the battlefield in the blink of an eye.
The Chronosphere is a long building, with the chronosphere device itself half-submerged underground, while being connected to an aboveground generator and control station. It has been improved many times over by SteinsTech through the years, such as enabling it to permanently teleport more than one vehicle, allow infantry within transports to be teleported safely, and theoretically reduce the chance of chrono vortexes appearing to zero. A small portion of its time-altering power can additionally be used to temporarily make vehicles move faster.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Clairvoyant
entries.content:
The Clairvoyant is the Foehn’s floating C-shaped infiltration drone, classified as infantry. Unlike other factions’ spies, it can’t disguise but compensates with low cost, amphibious movement, and Spinblade-boosted speed. Primarily a detector, it exposes stealth units and immobilizes them with a stun beam, letting allies finish the job. Though lacking offensive power, its scouting and anti-espionage role makes it invaluable for reconnaissance and securing areas against hidden threats.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Cloning Vat
entries.content:
Cloning used to be but a futuristic dream until Yuri turned it into a nightmarish reality. After defecting from the Soviets, Yuri took the technology for the Cloning Vats with him in order to quickly bolster his ranks. Producing near-perfect, and engineered for obedience clones of already trained soldiers allowed Epsilon to effectively double the size of their infantry divisions.
It is essentially A large vat connected to a control terminal with an attached ladder. Genetic template files are loaded into the terminal and the clone itself is fabricated within the vat, which he then exits through a side ladder.
They are used both by Epsilon and the Soviets in their Soyuz moonbase to replace their dwindled population numbers.
It is used by the moon-based Soviet Russia and all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Cloud Piercer
entries.content:
The Cloud Piercers are wide highly technological pillar structures with tall Cloud Piercer sensor towers protruding upwards from the base structure. The Revolt's staff within these towers monitors the behavior of winds nearby and perform complicated calculations, which allow their army to make the best use of its flow and employ the forces of nature in battle. The Cloud Piercer's data makes it possible to assess the best locations for the deployment of Spinblades, which will boost the speeds of units equipped with the windspin engines.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Coal plant
entries.content: Coal plant is essentially a large coal power plant.

entries.name: Colossus
entries.content:
the Colossus is Epsilon's towering heavy assault vehicle, combining strong armor with surprising mobility. Armed with psionic blaster cannons, it excels against ground targets while also serving as a deadly anti-air platform. Its unique dual AA guns shred aircraft, especially slow or stationary ones, dealing increased damage at close range. This versatility makes the Colossus a key asset against Allied and Soviet forces.
It is used by Epsilon HQ.

entries.name: Combat dolphin
entries.content:
One of the initially controversial, and then most successful ideas was an attempt of training Dolphins for usage in the Allied navy. Those nimble mammals were capable of swiftly scouting nearby areas, and if any threat was found, a system of sensors would immediately send enemy coordinates to nearby units.
To amplify potential of Dolphins they have been equipped with another type of Comet Prism weapons, which are mounted on their backs. With those, they could attempt to engage not only enemies on waters, but also take down some targets at the shores.
It is used by all three Allied  Subfactions.

entries.name: Concrete bunker
entries.content: The Concrete Bunker is a well protected neutral defensive structure that can be garrisoned by troops like that of civilian structures around the battlefield, giving it some degree of flexibility and modularity. Bunkers are important fortifications for the infantry to shelter in, and fire from. These special Concrete Bunkers have been constructed to withstand quite a lot of damage of any kind, and can even be repaired.

entries.name: Concrete fortress
entries.content: The Concrete Fortress is a neutral defensive structure that is basically a much larger version of Tech Concrete Bunkers, being twice as durable. An immense and tall fortification, the Concrete Fortress is capable of housing an entire infantry battalion. Impressive in size and durability, they are often a vital defense at strategic locations and choke points.

entries.name: Condor
entries.content:
The Condor is the Last Bastion’s armored Buzzard variant, optimized for base defense. Trading speed for heavy plating, it replaces it's internal stun mines with a microwave blaster—devastating against infantry but useless against aircraft.
Its hit-and-run tactic involves blasting infantry first, then engaging with integrated heavy machine guns (IHMGs). While slower, it excels in crowd control for fortified positions.
It is used by the Last Bastion.

entries.name: Conscript
entries.content:
Conscripts are men, most often clones created from cloning vats formerly used by lunar Epsilon forces, drafted into service for the Soviet armies. With Soviet forces pressured to churn out an ever increasing amount of troops, Conscripts are often poorly equipped and only have the most basic military training. They are very cost effective however and are often trained en masse for use in human wave tactics. They usually wear long brown trenchcoats with steel SSH-68 helmets, gas masks and wield PPSH-41 submachineguns.
they are used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Coronia
entries.content:
Coronia is a massive flying Foehn-built fortress loosely modelled off the destroyed Paradox Engine. It also functions as gigantic floating airbase of the Foehn Revolt that shields the troops located within with it's own, smaller Time Bubble. To further protect itself, it is constantly surrounded by an artificially generated hurricane, courtesy of it's onboard wind manipulation technology that exceeds that of any known application of said technology.
It also serves as home for the third Foehn subfaction, the so-called Wings of Coronia, which is essentially the Foehn Revolt's airforce that specializes in: Aerial supremacy, advanced area-of-effect weaponry and wind manipulation technology.

entries.name: Cosmonaut
entries.content:
Cosmonauts are the Soyuz Moonbase's equivalent of territorial guard, equipped with all the necessary life support equipment to survive in the vacuum of space and a jet pack packed inside of a white space suit like that permits them not just to walk across the moon's surface, but to also fly above it.
They are used by Soviet Russia.

entries.name: Crazy Ivan
entries.content:
Crazy Ivan is the umbrella term for the infantry divisions in the Soviet armies that specialize in demolition and wholesale destruction. The explosives Crazy Ivans use are entirely self-made, time-triggered incendiary explosives. Having the Ivans create their own bombs with barely any safety procedures provides an unintended and rather unorthodox method of rooting out incompetence.
Unfortunately, the possibility of having your own weapons spontaneously explode at any time has taken its psychological toll on the Ivans, making them perhaps a bit too anxious to rid themselves of their bombs. Crazy Ivans are trained to swim, carrying their explosives in protective plastic bags.
They are used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Cryocopter
entries.content:
The Cryocopter is a three-tailed Allied support helicopter capable of freezing enemies to stop them in their tracks and make them fragile using it's powerful freezing ray.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Cryomines
entries.content:
The Cryomines are special landmines used by the Pacific Front.
While the Cryomines' uniquely mixed cryo charge combined with a light explosive doesn't deal a lot of damage to enemy units on its own, and is not capable of completely immobilizing them in place like the other cryo-based weaponry, it is still very effective in disrupting enemy formations. The charge causes a rapid but short-lasting deep freeze, which results in a simultaneous decrease of the affected objects' armor and speed.
They are used by the Pacific Front.

entries.name: Cyberkernel
entries.content:
To expand their network of influence beyond the Last Bastion's territory, the Foehn Revolt aims to construct more Cyberkernels around the world. These structures are massive open-air server rooms coonected to a radar control builing that serve as Foehn's intelligence collection hubs, communication centers and supercomputers in one, making them an important target for the Revolt's enemies. In addition to enabling some of the advanced technology, the Cyberkernel provides access to the radar and the scouting support power in the form of Recon Sortie, which summons two drones that will reveal the shroud in a straight line of their flight over the battlefield.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Cyborg vanguard
entries.content:
The Cyborg Vanguard is a Chinese (technology later taken and used by Russia, however) heavy infantry unit. These towering soldiers clad in body armor are based from the same cybernetic technology that created Volkov and is a menacing presence to be encountered in the battlefield.
They are tall and imposing cyborgs clad in heavy power armor, wearing wide, flat conical metal helmets and gas masks permanently bolted to their face. They are armed with chainguns and high explosive grenades.
It is used by Soviet Russia.

entries.name: Cyclops walker
entries.content:
The Cyclops Walker is a battle walker armed with a single 110mm main cannon used by Haihead that fills the role of a main battle tank, despite being a different classification of vehicle.
It is used by Haihead.

entries.name: Demolition truck
entries.content:
The Demolition Truck is a bomb truck carrying a powerful B.O.O.M. warhead used by Soviet factions. It is usually used in suicide attacks as an effective method of quickly delivering a high explosive warhead straight ot the enemy's doorstep.
It is used by Soviet Russia and China.

entries.name: Desolator
entries.content:
The Desolator is a radioactive nightmare in human form. Clad in protective armor, he wields a shoulder-mounted radiation cannon that liquefies infantry and damages even heavy vehicles. He can also deploy his cannon, creating lethal radioactive zones that poison the terrain. A walking ecological disaster, he turns battlefields into toxic wastelands.
They are used by Soviet Russia and the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: Deviatress
entries.content:
The Deviatress is the upgraded version of the Huntress created when one is infused by a Nanofiber Sync. Trading their nanoid gun and hijacking ability for better, more darker-colored armor and a confusion rifle, they can break enemy formations by causing ground and air units alike to become unable to differentiate friend or foe, and attacks each other in confusion.
They are used by It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Diverbee
entries.content:
The Diverbee is a flying kamikaze drone used by Haihead to destroy enemy vehicles and aircraft in fast, surprise attacks.
It is used by Haihead.

entries.name: Draco light tank
entries.content:
The Draco Light Tank is the main battle tank of the Wings of Coronia.
The key piece in the Draco's design, however, is the ability to release its turret as an autonomous flying drone, in case of the vehicle's demise. When this tank is destroyed, the Autoturret will activate its own engines and detach from the main body, ascending to the sky to continue the fight from above. These drones won't withstand much damage, but might be enough to give the Foehn commanders the advantage, especially when their enemies possess scarce anti-air weapons
It is used by Wings of Coronia.

entries.name: Dragonfly
entries.content:
The Dragonfly is a flying Chinese support drone used to immobilize enemy vehicles with quick EMP immobilizer rays, opening them up for Chinese tanks to destroy.
It is used by China.

entries.name: Drakuv Prison Vehicle
entries.content:
The Drakuv Prison Vehicle is a Soviet heavy multi-functional carrier, blending support and specialized tactics. Its massive front grinder immobilizes and shreds anything it encounters—even enemy tanks—until halted or destroyed. Turrets atop the crawler fire tranquilizer darts, enabling the capture and brainwashing of weakened infantry into Soviet service or delivery to the Field Bureau. Additionally, the Drakuv supplies health packs, healing nearby troops and restoring injured soldiers to combat readiness. A formidable hybrid of offense and utility, it exemplifies ruthless Soviet engineering.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Driller
entries.content:
Drillers are Epsilon's primary armored personnel carriers, with a twist. The Driller is equipped with a large, tungsten-coated titanium drill on the front, allowing it to quickly tunnel into the earth and avoid enemies and terrain obstacles altogether. Though this gives the Driller the ultimate element of surprise, it can only carry up to three passengers and is completely unarmed. The Driller's armor, though strong enough to withstand the dangers of subterranean travel, offers little resistance to enemy fire.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Dugan
entries.content: President Dugan was elected before the Third World War. When the Soviets attacked, he failed to negotiate peace with Premier Romanov and ordered a nuclear counterstrike—thwarted by Yuri’s psychic control. Fleeing to Texas, Dugan relocated to The Alamo but was forced to escape when Latin Confederation forces attacked. His attempt to reach a military airport failed after Soviet strikes destroyed it. Redirecting to a civilian airstrip, he was fatally shot by Morales mid-escape. With his death, the U.S. collapsed, though scattered military remnants endured.

entries.name: Dunerider
entries.content:
Acting in loose groups as quick response teams to any threat that may compromise the security of Epsilon settlements, Duneriders are tan uniform-clad Epsilon scouts that use anti-gravity hover boards that allow them to maneuver across any terrain with extreme ease and great speed. Lobbing grenades with toxic charges makes the Dunerider an effective jack-of-all-trades to infantry and buildings. They wear full-body tan jumpsuit with a purple vest an a black balaclava on their heads.
They are used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Duplicant
entries.content:
When Nanofiber Sync transforms a Clairvoyant, it becomes a Duplicant—a nanite-driven bug-like drone that invades the bodies of enemy infantry. Unlike its scout-focused predecessor, the Duplicant consumes soldiers to fuel its endless replication. After attacking, it disassembles to seek new hosts; failure means permanent disintegration. Successful strikes trigger chain reactions, as one Duplicant can harvest multiple victims. Its entire structure is optimized for relentless multiplication, making it a terrifying bio-mechanical plague. However, this hunger comes with risk—if cut off from new hosts, the nanites cannot reform, ending the threat.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Dustdevil
entries.content:
The Dustdevil is a Soviet v-shaped support bomber that can weaken enemies through its smoke bombing runs.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Dybbuk
entries.content:
The Dybbuk, Epsilon’s unconventional aircraft series, features six distinct variants—each with unique battlefield roles. Three are standard production models: the widely used Attacker and Evolver, plus the rarely seen Seizer. The other three require special deployment: the Interceptor (carried by Psicorps' Gehenna Platforms), the toxin-bombing Striker (summoned by Scorpion Cell), and the Transport (exclusive to Psicorps for deploying Libra clones). With atypical weaponry and varied combat functions, Dybbuks defy conventional aerial doctrines, making them unpredictable threats in Epsilon’s arsenal.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Dybbuk Attacker
entries.content:
The Dybbuk-Attacker is a member of Epsilon's Dybbuk series of aircraft, serving as an anti-armor fighter. It is armed with two anti-armor ARO launchers
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Dybbuk Interceptor
entries.content:
The Dybbuk-Interceptor is a member of Epsilon's Dybbuk series of aircraft, serving as an anti-air fighter. It often appears along with the Gehenna Platform or Dybbuk Hive.
Dybbuk Hives are special 'buildings' used by the Epsilon Army to churn out an unlimited amount of Dybbuk-Interceptors.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Dybbuk-Evolver
entries.content:
The Dybbuk-Evolver is yet another member of Epsilon's Dybbuk series of aircraft, with this one functioning as a bomber, whose genobombs are capable of mutating unfortunate infantry caught in its bombing runs into Brutes.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: EMP control station
entries.content:
Due to their chosen technological path and strategy, the Chinese put large emphasis on their EMP technology. The EMP Control Station has been designed with one purpose in mind: to stop the faster enemy tanks which are trying to outmaneuver the slow Chinese machines in one spot. By directing enough energy into this building, the Chinese are capable of creating an effective EM Pulse anywhere on the battlefield whenever the weapon has fully charged by sending the signal to one of their satellites equipped with an EM projector. The pulse created with this device has the largest area effect of all EMP weapons that the Chinese have developed so far.
It is used by China

entries.name: EMP mines
entries.content:
Chinese EMP Mines are simple defenses used at choke points or other important locations. Though the blast of a Mine can kill or heavily injure infantry, the most prominent feature is that it can disable enemy vehicles for a significant amount of time. Either giving a chinese commander more time to set up his defenses, or acting as a trap on the path of unsuspecting enemies, the EMP Mines are a contraption to be feared.
They are used by all China.

entries.name: Engineer
entries.content:
The Engineer is a crucial infantry unit for all factions, tasked with repairing friendly structures, capturing enemy/neutral buildings by rewiring electronics, defusing explosives, repairing bridges, and securing empty vehicles. They can also repair vehicles when inside an IFV or Stinger. While their role is the same across factions, their uniforms and equipment vary in appearance and design. Despite being unarmed and unable to fix mechanical units alone, Engineers are highly valuable on the battlefield. 
It is used by all Factions and subfactions.

entries.name: Enterprise Aircraft Carrier
entries.content:
The Enterprise-class Aircraft Carrier is one of the most powerful ships the Allies have to offer. Packing several drones capable of delivering their payload over huge distances with deadly accuracy, this floating airbase is capable of leveling any enemy base to the ground with ease. Due to the precise nature of its attacks, the Enterprise can hold its own in direct combat. The Enterprise's UAVs can,however, be shot down by enemy anti-aircraft fire, and thus make the ship vulnerable to retaliation from the seas.
It is used by all three Alied Subfactions.

entries.name: Epsilon Adept
entries.content:
The very core members of Yuri's Epsilon Army and the successors of the original decades-old Soviet PsiCorps division, the Adepts are individuals with above average psychic abilities, allowing them to bend the will of others to suit their goals. They pose a significant threat to almost all soldiers and human-operated vehicles, turning their victims against their compatriots with a mere thought.
Adepts are capable of defending themselves against infantry with a potent psychic blast which overwhelms the brains of unshielded soldiers caught within, resulting in death. Though powerful opponents, Adepts are not able to control the minds of animals and are completely defenseless against robotic units. They wear grey Epsilon Army uniforms with tan pants and unzipped grey overcoats. For some reason, most of them are bald. Following the activation of the Mental Omega Device, they became the equivalent of lower aristocracy in a new, Epsilon-dominated world.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Epsilon Aerodrome
entries.content:
Just like the Allies build their Air Force Command Headquarters and the Soviets have begun deploying Airbases once again, the Epsilon's forces have designed an airfield of their own. The Aerodome is where they construct, maintain and reload the aircraft from their Dybbuk series.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Epsilon Army
entries.content:
The Epsilon Army, led by Yuri, evolved from Stalin's PsiCorps. It aimed to enforce global mind control. Epsilon's forces included PsiCorps, Epsilon HQ, and Scorpion Cell. Its arsenal featured mind control, genetic corruption, and bioweapons. Despite Yuri's death, Libra activated the Mental Omega Device, enslaving Earth under a psychic hivemind. Only Point Hope remains free. The device merged Epsilon's subfactions: Scorpion Cell, PsiCorps, and Epsilon HQ, into one, solidifying their control over the world. Epsilon now dominates Earth through its psychic hivemind imposed by the Mental Omega Device.
Their buildings and equipment have a much more sinister, cyberpunk and brass aesthetic with their main colors being purple, magenta, lime, dark purple, pink and dark green.

entries.name: Epsilon Elite
entries.content:
The Elite force of the Epsilon Army, Adepts who have attained further psychic power and who have proven their worth to Yuri himself. Assigned to the PsiCorps, they represent some of Yuri's most powerful agents. Emanating such powerful psychic energies gives the Elite minor telekinetic abilities as they levitate themselves slightly above the ground, allowing Elites to travel over water. They wear the grey overcoat uniforms of Epsilon adepts, but with purple and gold shoulder tabs, signifying their higher rank. Just like all Adepts, they are completely bald. Following the activation of the Mental Omega Device, they became the aristocracy of the new world, now below only Rahn and the Proselyte.
They are primarily used by Epsilon HQ.

entries.name: Epsilon HQ
entries.content: The Epsilon Headquarters is Yuri’s elite defense force based in Antarctica, tasked with guarding his secret superweapon. Known for advanced tech and genetic experiments, they produced mutant soldiers, stealth weapons, and the Aerial Fortress Irkalla. Initially limited to defensive roles, they later expanded into Asia and Africa, clashing with Allied and Chinese forces. Despite setbacks like the Kashmir disaster and the Paradox Engine, they played key roles in major battles. During the final stages of the Mental Omega War, Epsilon HQ helped repel Allied forces, ultimately defending Yuri’s Tower, though some Allied remnants escaped.

entries.name: Epsilon Shipyard
entries.content:
A must on any battlefield with large bodies of water. The Epsilon Naval Shipyard allows for the construction of Epsilon ships and submersibles, and easily repairs any damaged vessels.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Epsilon Spook
entries.content:
Spooks are twisted genetically engineered foating creatures serving as Epsilon's reconnaissance unit, basically serving as a grotesque counterpart to the Allied and Soviet Attack Dogs.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Epsilon War Factory
entries.content:
The Epsilon War Factory allows for the production of the Epsilon's varied and often bizarre war machines on the battlefield. What strange technologies are used to produce these strange vehicles is anyone's guess.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Epslilon Barracks
entries.content:
The Epsilon Barracks is a shrine dedicated to Yuri's vision, even so far as to be built in the likeness of his head. Yuri's voice constantly echoes through the structure, bringing confidence and bravery to those who serve him. Epsilon infantry live and train within their barracks.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Eradicator
entries.content:
Where the Desolator was already an irresponsible effort to create a powerful infantry unit, the Chinese take it a step further in the form of the Eradicator. The Eradicator carries an experimental, even more lethal radiation cannon. So much in fact, that it constantly leaks radiation, thus making the Eradicator dangerous at all times to surrounding units. Like the Desolator, the Eradicator can deploy in order to irradiate the earth, however, his spread of irradiation is much bigger.
They are used by China.

entries.name: Eureka
entries.content:
Eureka is a cheerful woman in her late 20's with wavy,blonde hair and green eyes. She is a mysterious yet formidable Coronian heroine who emerged suddenly and quickly proved her battlefield dominance. She wears a distinctive Foehn uniform with a dark green scarf and wields devastating plasma weaponry. Her primary armament consists of a circular plasma generator with twin powerful blasters, capable of generating massive shockwaves that obliterate light armor and severely damage heavier units. The weapon's intense green flashes often mark enemies' final moments, making tank divisions retreat at her approach.
Due to her weapon's uncontrollable nature, Eureka typically operates alone to avoid friendly fire. However, she can rapidly rejoin allies using her windspin-enhanced boots, which harness Spinblade-generated winds for sudden speed bursts. This combination of overwhelming firepower and mobility has cemented her reputation as one of Coronia's most feared combatants, though her isolationist tactics reflect both the weapon's power and its dangerous unpredictability.
She belongs to the Wings oF Coronia.

entries.name: European Alliance
entries.content: The Euro Alliance, a defensive alliance of European nations, backed by advanced tech from SteinsTech—led by Einstein's protégé Siegfried—relied on chrono, weather, prism, and mirage weaponry. Formed after the Second Great War to counter Soviet threats, the Alliance emphasized defense and tech innovation. Despite early resistance in the Third Great War, they lost most of Europe to the Soviets, retaining only the UK. In the Mental Omega War, they led the Allied Nations, recovering key tech and fighting major battles in Europe, Cape Town, and Antarctica. Their forces played pivotal roles but were ultimately overwhelmed and failed to destroy the Mental Omega Device, and the Euro Alliance ceased to exist after the fall of the London Fortress. with it's remnants having become incorporated into the Foehn Revolt, while Europe and the rest of the world became enslaved by the Mental Omega Device.

entries.name: Experimental warpshop
entries.content:
The Experimental Warpshop is a high-tech Allied structure, acting as a nexus for the development and creation of allied chrono technology.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Field Bureau
entries.content:
The Field Bureau is an important Soviet intelligence building. Construction of this structure marks the first step of a local technology advancement for basic weapon branches. But the most important feature of these is the capability to imprison and research the weapons of the enemies.
Using the Drakuv Prison Vehicle, which is housed within the Bureau, it is possible to capture enemy soldiers and move them into this building in order to analyze the weapons and equipment they are using.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Field Medic
entries.content:
Even with all their armor and training, an Allied soldier doesn't last very long in combat without support. On the battlefield, where every man counts, the allied Field Medic is there to keep the troops alive as long as possible. They are usually unarmed,however.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Flak Cannon
entries.content:
The Flak Cannon is the premier Soviet anti-aircraft defense. The cannon lobs numerous large flak shells from four autocannons at incredible speeds towards incoming aerial targets. Once the shell hits a target, it explodes into smaller pellets, shredding other nearby aircraft
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Flak troopers
entries.content:
Flak Troopers are the main anti-armor and anti-aircraft infantry of the Soviet armies. The position of Flak Trooper is one of the lowest in the Soviet army, even compared to the Conscript divisions. Former convicts or the homeless were gathered in massive training camps to get crash courses on how to use their personal shoulder-fired flak cannons. Their "payment" for service in the army is generally either housing and food or freedom after the war. Needless to say, not many men live long enough to see that payment.
They are  used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Foehn barracks
entries.content:
The unusually extensive Foehn Barracks are a gate to their underground facilities, where most of the Revolt's infantry training and weapon assembling is taking place. These uniquely designed Barracks provide housing and training facilities to basic and advanced Foehn infantry.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Foehn Leadership council
entries.content:
the Feohn leadership council is essentially the ruling government of the Foehn Revolt and their base in Point Hope.
Current members: Yunru, Rashidi, Tanya Adams, General Carville.

entries.name: Foehn naval shipyard
entries.content:
The Foehn Naval Shipyard is a large and lengthy floating building that allows for the construction of Foehn ships and submersibles, and easily repairs any damaged vessels.
It is used by all three Foehn  Subfactions.

entries.name: Foehn Revolt
entries.content: The Foehn Revolt, led by Yunru, emerged from Chinese defectors and scientists aiming to challenge Russian and Epsilon dominance. After escaping Epsilon captivity, Yunru allied with Scorpion Cell and used a stolen MIDAS warhead in battle. Evacuating to Alaska, the Revolt joined forces with Allied remnants and activated the Paradox Engine to shield Point Hope from Epsilon's mind control. Inside the time bubble, they fused various global technologies to prepare for a final resistance. Foehn's doctrine emphasizes tech superiority, using plasma railguns, wind-based weapons, and cybernetic troops. Their sleek highly technological neon aesthetic defines their three subfactions: Last Bastion, Wings of Coronia, and Haihead.

entries.name: Foehn subfaction building addons
entries.content:
To acquire a complete access to their advanced technologies, each of the Foehn Revolt's subfaction armies wtihin a specific area must upgrade their nearest technology building which corresponds to its technology and strategy choice. This is why Haihead will aim to construct an Expansion for the Cyberkernel, the Wings of Coronia will upgrade the Cloud Piercer, and the Last Bastion will focus on developing an addition to the Nanofiber Loom.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Foehn War Factory
entries.content:
The Foehn War Factory allows for the production of Foehn's expensive and technologically advanced units on the battlefield. It is also the only place where the Foehn Revolt can construct its aircraft at, since they do not require an airfield for such units to land and reload at, due to their capabilities of controlling the winds.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Foehn whipray
entries.content:
The Whipray is Foehn's new claw-shaped naval drone, specializing in anti-air defense. As the first mass-produced crewless ship, it resists Epsilon mind control. Its durable design sacrifices a turret for survivability. Armed with a "Golden Rocket" launcher and a confusion rifle tailored for aircraft, it also leverages a windspin engine, boosted by Spinblades and SODAR Arrays to enhance projectile performance.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Foxtrot
entries.content:
The Foxtrot is a jet fighter used by the Soviets, armed with Scorch missiles, it not only cripples the main target, but also sets fire around it as well, dealing consistent damage to units and structures nearby. The weapon also hits multiple targets at a time, making them even more effective against formations. With decent armor and relatively high speed, the Foxtrot is a force to reckon with.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Fury drone
entries.content:
The Fury Drone is a quadropedal kamikaze drone used by the Latin Confederation, which burrows into the ground and lies in wait until an enemy gets close, at which it will surprise them by leaping onto the unfortunate enemy before exploding.
It is used by the Latin Confederation.

entries.name: FutureTech
entries.content:
FutureTech emerged from SteinsTech and Kanegawa Industries after the U.S. fell, developing the Weather Controller from a hidden Virgin Islands base. Allied forces rescued Kanegawa's chrono-tech scientists for the Paradox Project, but a sabotaged chronoshift diverted them to Europe's Black Forest base. Though Soviets destroyed it with a MIDAS missile, the scientists escaped.
After defending the U.K., FutureTech rebuilt the Chronosphere over two years. When Yuri's Epsilon Army attacked London, the Paradox Engine launched prematurely, stranding FutureTech personnel aboard. Meanwhile, the completed Weather Controller was secured by Allies, and FutureTech's Pacific forces rejoined the expedition.

entries.name: Gap Generator
entries.content:
The Gap Generator is a remarkable piece of Allied technology, which is a tall high-tech tower, with the gap generator itself located at the very top. It constantly regenerates a large amount of shroud around the structure, effectively hiding anything nearby from the prying eyes of enemies.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Gatling cannon
entries.content:
Gatling Cannons are the primary defense emplacement of all Epsilon forces. A versatile and powerful rotary cannon capable of pumping out several thousand rounds a minute, it functions as both the main anti-infantry and anti-aircraft defense. Though this dual purpose gives it a major advantage over its Allied and Soviet counterparts, it requires power to operate, making an Epsilon base much more dependant on a constant power source to protect itself from enemies.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Gatling Tank
entries.content:
When the potential of gatling weaponry became apparent, it was only logical that the cannons would eventually be mounted on a tank. The Gatling Tank is able to train its guns on ground targets, proving that not only is a hail of bullets effective against aircraft armor, but devastating against targets of the soft and fleshy variety as well. Unfortunately, the tank's effectiveness against armored units is minimal.
Despite being called a tank, the Epsilon Gatling Tank is in actuality a four-wheeled armored car with twin gatling cannons within it's turret.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Gehenna Platform
entries.content:
The Gehenna Platform is PsiCorps' mobile anti-aircraft system, mounting a Dybbuk-Interceptor on a slow but heavily tracked chassis. Equipped with long-range tracking, it launches autonomous missiles that relentlessly hunt aircraft until destroyed, out of ammo, or if the Gehenna itself is taken out. While unmatched in air defense, its sluggish speed leaves it vulnerable to ground attacks. This makes it a high-risk, high-reward weapon—dominant against air threats but dependent on protection from other units.
It is used by PsiCorps.

entries.name: General Carville
entries.content:
A chubby man in his early 40's, General Carville was meant to be retired during the period before Third Great War breaks out. When the Soviets invaded Washington D.C., he had to rejoin the U.S. Army and act as the leadership at the Pentagon.
After the defeat of the United States, he is not captured by the Soviets but continue commanding remaining forces to resist. Two years later, he commanded several remaining divisions to retake Washington D.C., which was already called as Stalington by the Soviets, but failed due to the intervention of Yuri's newly-founded Epsilon Army.
He managed to escape after the battle, and it is later revealed that he is hiding along with what is left of the American Forces in Point Hope Fortress.

entries.name: Genomines
entries.content:
The Genomines are landmines used by the Epsilon Headquarters. When triggered, they release a mutagenic gas that will mutate enemy infantry exposed to it into Brutes.
They are used by Epsilon HQ.

entries.name: Gharial
entries.content:
The Gharial is a versatile Last Bastion Infantry fighting vehicle, complementing the Mastodon with balanced armor and speed. Armed with a dual imploder-penetrator cannon (like Kingsframes) and HE grenade launchers contained within an unmanned turret at it's back, it excels against ground targets and structures. Its amphibious hull doubles as a troop transport, carrying 3 pre-loaded Knightframes per doctrine.
it's four-wheeled chassis is its crowning achievement—immune to EMP, radiation, poison, freezing, confusion, and mind control—thanks to decades of advanced engineering.
It is used by the Last Bastion

entries.name: Ghost Miner
entries.content: The ghost miner is a half-tracked miner vehicle that is used by all three factions of the Epsilon Army. The Epsilon Ghost Miner has a unique cloaking defense using a Chimera Core, similar to Shadow Tanks. However, its heavy mining equipment demands more power, causing temporary cloak failure during energy spikes and exposing it to enemies.

entries.name: GI
entries.content:
