entries.name: Rocketeer
entries.content:
Rocketeers are brave individuals who hover far above the battlefield on their jetpacks, engaging ground and air targets with relative impunity via machineguns attached to the wrists of their rocketeer suit. Though their high speed and maneuverability makes them excellent scouts, they are very vulnerable to anti-air emplacements.
They are used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Runway
entries.content: The Runway is a simple landing strip, allowing aircraft to land and resupply.

entries.name: Russia
entries.content:
During the Third Great War, Soviet Russia aggressively targeted the Allies, achieving major victories in the U.S., Europe, and Asia. They used Psychic Beacons and MIDAS missiles, but setbacks arose when China turned against them, leading to internal conflict. Despite reclaiming dominance with threats of Topol-Ms (later revealed as empty), Russia faced Yuri’s betrayal—losing Moscow and Stalington to mind control. Survivors like Reznov and Krukov resisted, sabotaging PsiCorps facilities. After a shaky truce with China collapsed, Russia acquired Chinese tech, defeated and took over Epsilon's base on the Moon, and killed Yuri in Moscow—only to unknowingly fall victim to his global Mental Omega Device, leaving only lunar Soviets free.
Their armies specialize in cybernetic infantry, field production and tesla weaponry.

entries.name: Saboteur
entries.content:
The Saboteur's main role is espionage: stealing important intelligence from enemy labs and facilities. Able to disguise himself as enemy infantry and slip past defenses, he is similar in that aspect to an Allied Spy. There is one major difference between the Saboteur and your regular espionage agent.
The Saboteur wears a vest with a low-yield bomb embedded within. The bomb's trigger is directly connected to a small heart rate monitor, which detonates the bomb when the Saboteur's heart stops. This contraption results in a localized explosion in the event the Saboteur is discovered and killed, either grievously wounding or killing the attacker.
They are used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: SAM bunker
entries.content: The SAM Bunker is a neutral defensive structure equipped with six heavy "Mauler" AA missiles that, when captured by an Engineer, is a superior version of the Tech SAM Site. Unlike the Tech SAM Site, it consumes some base power. Tech SAM Bunkers are massive anti-air defenses, which can easily take down almost any aerial threat at great ranges. This powerful defensive structure's only weakness is that it requires quite a bit of power.

entries.name: SAM site
entries.content: The SAM Site is a neutral defensive structure equipped with six surface-to-air "Redeye missiles" that, when captured, is basically a surface-to-air (SAM) missile site able to engage aircraft effectively.

entries.name: Satellite hack center
entries.content: The Satellite Hack Center is a neutral structure that, when captured, grants the owner a full battlefield view through the newly developed Global Positioning System (GPS). However, should the structure is destroyed or change control, its (previous) owner will completely lose their view of the battlefield except of their own forces.

entries.name: Scorpion Cell
entries.content:
The Scorpion Cell, led by Rashidi, waged guerrilla warfare against Allied/Soviet forces in Africa/Middle East using scavenged tech. Allied with Yuri, they destroyed targets in Cairo and sabotaged Chinese psychotrons. After aiding Epsilon's Russian conquest, Rashidi's secret pact with Yunru caused rebellion against Epsilon. Allied attacks and internal betrayal decimated the group - most were absorbed into Epsilon's hivemind when Mental Omega activated. Rashidi himself escaped to Point Hope, while Malver continued his solo operations against Epsilon in Africa. The Cell's remnants now serve as mind-controlled Epsilon shock troops.
They specialize in numerical superiority, hit-and-run tactics and the usage of chemical weapons

entries.name: Scourge
entries.content:
With Rashidi's personal training and advanced weapon-crafting talents, the Scourges joined his ranks after the Scorpion Cell suffered a series of severe losses to heavy enemy armor on its own home territories. The custom weapon he is equipped with is extremely destructive to tanks, although its shots cannot be concentrated at a single point due to its strong recoil, making it a rather inaccurate weapon.
The key characteristic of the Scourge's weapon is that, shockingly to the Cell's enemies, it actually makes use of a short EMP effect.The scourges wear heavy and bulky exosuit-amplified armor with a special mask that protects their face from shrapnel.|
It is used by Scorpion Cell.

entries.name: Scout Raven
entries.content:
Scout ravens are genetically modified ravens fully controlled by Epsilon commanders. They are used for efficient scouting and surveillance by Epsilon forces.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Scud launcher
entries.content:
The Scud Launcher is a tracked mobile loading and launching platform for tactical ballistic missiles. As is customary of the Soviet philosophy, firepower and armor are emphasized with this powerful siege engine, making it one of the most powerful long-range threats on the battlefield. A few direct hits from a Scud Launcher will cause even the sturdiest of buildings to collapse into a pile of rubble.
Unfortunately, due to the relatively slow speed of the projectile the missile can be shot down by anti-aircraft defenses. Another drawback is that even though the Scud Launcher is one of the heaviest armored artilleries, it is still vulnerable to enemy fire and shouldn't be left undefended.
It is used by Russia.

entries.name: Seawolf
entries.content:
Lacking an anti-aircraft ship in the previous war, the Soviets developed a fast sea raider known as the Seawolf Gunboat, capable of quickly destroying aircraft and harassing other ships. This multi-purpose attack craft has proven to be one of the Soviets more versatile naval vessels. Its turreted quad flak cannons and high caliber machinegun allow the Seawolf to engage both land and air targets.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Second Great War
entries.content: The Second Great War or GWII, also known as the Second World War or WWII, was a major armed conflict that began in 1946 and ended in 1953. It marks the first time where the Allies fought with the Soviets. The Allies were ultimately victorious at the end of the war, and the leader of the Soviets during that time, Stalin, was killed.

entries.name: Secret lab
entries.content: The Secret Lab contains unique technological concepts, designed by various weapon development groups, who sought independence from the warring nations' influence. Once captured, this building will grant you access to these engineers' latest invention, the support aircraft Rejuvenator.

entries.name: Seitaad Ballista
entries.content:
The Seitaad Ballista is wide, long, yet flat artillery vehicle whose design merges Soviet EMP tech with Foehn nanofiber threads, creating a deadly hybrid weapon. Its area-of-effect EMP (like China's EMP Control Station) disables multiple targets, leaving them vulnerable to armor-piercing nanofiber barrages (similar to Last Bastion's tech). This dual-phase attack shreds armor and structures effortlessly, making the Ballista a near-flawless siege weapon.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Sensor tower
entries.content:
The Soviet Sensor Tower was developed after Yuri's betrayal to counter his psi-tech. It reveals hidden threats—including invisible units, explosives, and spies—while its spotlight exposes enemies for increased damage.
Crucially, it disrupts enemy scouting abilities, blocking reconnaissance powers in its radius. A vital defense against deception, it safeguards Soviet bases from both psychological warfare and covert ops.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.content:
Aside from Halftracks, China lacked a dedicated advanced anti-aircraft system to protect their "crawling wall" of tanks. Filling this gap is the Sentinel, the guardian of the Chinese forces. Sentinels are sluggish six-wheeled vehicles whose two autocannons are loaded with modified white phosphor flak shells, which react violently with the air when impacting with a target, burning through metal in seconds. Being a specialized anti-aircraft weapon, the Sentinel can only fire upon aircraft in order to ensure maximum effectiveness.
It is used by China.

entries.name: Sentry gun
entries.content:
Sentry Guns are automated turrets outfitted with dual chain guns in order to combat enemy infantry and light vehicles. Though not equipped to deal with more heavily armored units, the Sentry Gun works well as a preliminary frontline defense of the Soviet outposts.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Shadow Tank
entries.content:
Epsilon HQ's triple-tracked Shadow Tank is a pinnacle of stealth warfare, using stolen Allied tech to remain permanently cloaked until firing its twin dissolver beams. Deadly against units (less so structures), it strikes unseen, forcing enemies to deploy detectors. A psychological terror weapon, it epitomizes Epsilon’s cunning—invisible, lethal, and unpredictable.
It is used by Epsilon HQ.

entries.name: Shadray torch tank
entries.content:
The Shadray Torch Tank is a revolutionary H-shaped four-tracked microwave weapon, born from enhanced sonic crystal technology. By combining and modifying four amplifier screens into a single powerful emitter, it generates devastating waves that penetrate even Blasticade defenses. Originally designed to incinerate infantry, vehicles, and structures, its unexpected anti-aircraft capability led to added targeting systems. This makes the Shadray both a long-range siege unit and air defense platform, far surpassing earlier microwave prototypes.
It is used by Haihead.

entries.name: Shield command
entries.content:
The European Alliance's Shield Command is a collection of one control room, a Force Shield generator and a lightning rod emergency generator, built on a round concrete base. It controls the Force Shield which can protect your structures from any sort of enemy attacks for a short while. It also provides the access to an emergency Lightning Rod, which is useful during power shortage situations.
It is used by European Alliance.

entries.name: Shock Trooper
entries.content:
In an ununsual call back to the original soldier, the new Russian Shock Trooper is their further improved version of the Tesla Trooper. He wears a thick armored exosuit, a stronger miniaturized tesla coil, and a rate of fire twice as fast as that of the Tesla Trooper. In addition, his bolt is capable of hitting more than one target.
These characteristics make the Shock Troopers appear more effective in countering larger numbers of enemy armor units in combat. Naturally, the Shock Troopers can also charge a Tesla Coil to enhance its bolt power and provide a short-term EMP effect, as well as benefit from the Overcharge.
It is used by Russia.

entries.name: Shrike nest
entries.content:
The Shrike Nest is the Foehn's ambush-style AA defense—a hidden drone bunker that launches Shrike drones when enemies enter range. These compact hunters fire "Golden Rockets", then return to reload.
Unlike static AA, Shrikes pursue targets beyond their nest's range, relentlessly attacking until ammo runs out or the aircraft is destroyed. This persistent chase makes them deadlier than conventional AA, forcing foes to either eliminate the nest or face inescapable retaliation.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Siege Cadre
entries.content:
The Siege Cadre is an Allied anti-structure infantry unit armed with a prism rifle, which is a smaller version of the Prism Tank's weapon, and wears thick, white, futurisitc armor with a full helmet which makes them immune to bites, scratches and makes them extra resistant against shrapnel..
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Siegfried
entries.content:
Siegfried is a German scientist in his mid-40s and a former associate of Albert Einstein. While Einstein advocated peaceful applications of his technology, Siegfried believes in weaponizing it to defend the free world. He wears a white protective suit and pilots the Zeitgeist, a massive chrono-tech craft armed with an advanced weapon that generates unstable chrono vortices, devastating enemies at range.
He sacrificed himsefl during the allied retreat from Antarctica, buying enough time for the bulk of retreating allied forces to escape by teleporting to Point Hope with the usage of the Paradox Engine's wreckage. Ultimately, he was killed by Rahn.

entries.name: Signal Inhibitor
entries.content:
The Signal Inhibitor is a special ECM-based device installed upon a tall high-tech post that disrupts enemy scouting and targetting equipment, while blocking enemy transmissions of Foehn base coordinates.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Siren Frigate
entries.content:
Due to frequent battles against Yuri's submerged fleets, the Allies had to design a new element of their navy, to prevent his subs from submerging and disappearing before anyone could even react. Thus, their scientists pulled a concept of a more powerful version of the Chrono Legionnaire's weapon on a new ship.
Equipped with a neutron blaster, the Siren Frigate lures passing ships into danger. Based on Kanegawa Industries' negation field technology, a new type of passive defense has been developed exclusively for this ship. When under enemy fire, it can pull the neutron blaster back and release the "Negation Shield", turning any damage dealt to the Siren into a reconstructive effect. However, its long-term eruption will put the Siren in an overloaded state and continuously damage its interior systems.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Smoke turret
entries.content:
Among the additional weapons, unique to the Latin Confederation, which rely on creating smoke screen, comes the Smoke Turret. This simple but useful contraption launches volleys of smoke projectiles from two automatic mortars which blind their enemies if they do not possess adequate navigation equipment. The Smoke Turret is cheap, effective and has great range. With enough spread of the weapon it fires, it can easily decrease the combat potential of incoming enemies, including some of the artillery units.
It is used by all three Latin Confederation Subfactions.

entries.name: Sniper
entries.content:
The Sniper is a type of European infantry who specialize in taking out enemy infantry from a distance without exposing their location by their AWP high-caliber bolt-action sniper rifles.
They are used by European Alliance.

entries.name: SODAR array
entries.content:
Yuri’s psychic illusions, including cloaked and subterranean units, posed a major threat to Foehn forces, prompting the development of the SODAR Array—a mobile detection system using wind-profiling technology to identify hidden threats. By analyzing sound wave scattering, it detects invisible units, requiring deployment on land or water for full functionality. Additionally, it enhances "Golden Rockets" by providing wind data, improving flight path accuracy and damage output.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Sonic Emitter
entries.content:
The Sonic Emitter is Foehn's basic anti-infantry defensive turret. It is the only basic defense capable of firing through walls, thanks to the design of its weapon: a sonic wave, emitted through a uniquely crafted crystal, which amplifies its power and makes it deadly to enemy infantry and rather effective against light vehicles as well.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Soviet Airbase
entries.content:
Many long years have passed before the Soviets were able to restore their mighty airforce. Initially, during the Soviet invasion of the United States, the Red Army resorted to using giant blimps to bombard enemy positions from the skies but not many jets were seen. Finally after their attack on the American aeronautics complexes all over the country, necessary tech was acquired to develop the next-gen of Soviet jet fighters. The Soviet Airbase exists to produce and maintain them.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Soviet barracks
entries.content:
The towering statue of a Conscript that adorns this structure is meant to inspire awe and pride into any soldier serving the Soviet cause. A compact and instantly recognizable building, the soviet barracks house and provide training facilities to soviet infantry units.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Soviet naval shipyard
entries.content:
The Naval Shipyard is where the Soviet navy are assembled and maintained. It can also deploy naval mines around the battlefield as a deterrent to enemy ships.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Soviet Union
entries.content:
The Soviet Union (also known as the Soviets or the Comintern), was an economic, military and political alliance between various communist factions and governments in the world, led by Russia.
The Soviet Union consisted of three major members: Russia, the People's People of China (PRC), and the Latin Confederation.
Soviet militaries often fielded massive quantities of heavy tanks and infantry to overwhelm their enemies with firepower. They were also infamous for utilizing controversial weapons such as suicide bombers, nuclear weapons, and flamethrowers. While not as technologically advanced as the the other factions, the Soviet military has nevertheless scored many victories by simply overpowering their rivals with conventional weapons. Their buildings and equipment have a much more industrial and brutalistic aesthetic with their main colors being red, orange, tan, maroon, brown, crimson and yellow.
Following the activation of the Mental Omega Device, only the soviet russians who remained on their Soyuz Moonbase remained free, while both the remnants of China and the Latin Confederation succumbed to Epsilon's global mind control.

entries.name: Soviet war factory
entries.content:
Perhaps one of the most vital buildings for the Soviets. The War Factory allows the construction of a myriad of armored vehicles on the battlefield, which the Soviets use to steamroll their opponents.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Soyuz moonbase
entries.content: Formerly a secret Epsilon research base on the moon, the Soyuz moonbase has now become the last non-mind controlled territory of former soviet Russia. It is a sprawling network of camps, manufacturing facilities, former Epsilon cloning vats and research bases located on the moon and the home of the new soviet politbureau, the government of lunar Soviet Russia.

entries.name: Speeder Trike
entries.content:
In spite of its appearance as a little three-wheeled bike, the Speeder Trike is a deadly anti-armor unit in the hands of the Scorpion Cell. The Trike can easily outrange most conventional weaponry with its long-range RPG-S launcher and is quick enough to outmaneuver most vehicles, also capable of switching into firing its triple projectiles simultaneously at high altitudes, making it a formidable foe in combat. Its armor is less than stellar though, so it should avoid direct hits from anti-tank weaponry.
It is used by Scorpion Cell.

entries.name: Spinblade
entries.content:
The Spinblade is an air-deployed support beacon structure that is deployed from the air, following a command sent directly from the nearest Foehn Cloud Piercer. It is a device that makes nearby units with windspin engines to be able to accelerate at greater velocities, resulting in a significant increase to their movement speed.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Stalin's fist
entries.content:
Heavy armor has always been a focus point for Soviet military vehicles. This does bring several problems with logistics, as heavier units are slow and take longer to reach their destination, which can very much mean victory or defeat on the battlefield. The Russians came with a surprisingly complicated solution.
A massive vehicle based on mobile construction, the same technology used by the MCV's, that could deploy into an assembly line in order to produce vehicles from. This moving War Factory, named Stalin's Fist, allows russian armies to churn out tanks right on the doorstep of their enemies. Although these machines are expensive and very limited in numbers, they provide a unique strategic advantage to the Russians.
It is used by Russia.

entries.name: Stalker
entries.content:
Epsilon’s most successful genetic experiments, Stalkers are hulking, intelligent brutes armored in reinforced bulky full-body black suits with dual integrated weapons and six visor-holes on their round,spherical helmets. Their immense strength lets them wield the devastating "Meteor" cannon, collapsing structures with sheer firepower. A secondary arm-cannon drains psychic energy from enemies, slowing them while fueling nearby allies’ regeneration.
Tougher than their failed kin (like the Brutes), Stalkers serve as mobile artillery, unstoppable under Epsilon’s enhancements. Paired with melee infantry and HQ support, they form an overwhelming assault force—crushing defenses and draining foes into submission.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Stallion Transport
entries.content:
The large Stallion Transport helicopter is one of Sikorsky corporation's finest transport helicopters and a standard in all Allied armies. Its large passenger capacity, coupled with radar invisibility, allows it to easily insert infantry battalions behind enemy lines.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Steinstech
entries.content:
The SteinsTech is an advanced technology industrial firm of European Alliance, led by Germany, most famous for its chrono technology based on Einstein's research. Its founder and leader is Siegfried.
During the Third Great War, Euro Alliance forces using SteinsTech weapons like Thor Gunships resisted Soviet invasions. SteinsTech suffered devastating losses when Soviets destroyed four key facilities, including their main lab and Chronosphere, after intelligence leaks from Canada. Allied forces evacuated personnel to Britain before MIDAS strikes. There, they joined escaped Kanegawa Industries scientists to launch the Paradox Project - the Allies' ultimate weapon. After two years of development, an Epsilon attack forced early deployment. The Paradox Engine evacuated most UK-based Allied personnel, including SteinsTech and KI teams, aboard a massive airborne fortress designed by both institutes. This marked SteinsTech's transformation into FutureTech as they embarked on a new mission.

entries.name: Stinger
entries.content:
Another great Rashidi's invention, the Stinger, is an unmanned, robotic walker that crawls on four mechanical limbs and is used to swiftly transport infantry across the battlefield. Though it can only transport a single infantry, the Stinger makes up for it in versatality, armed with an acid sprayer to decimate infantry with and lightly damage vehicles.
Along with sensors to detect stealth and disguises, the Stinger functions as the Epsilon's main repair vehicle when an Engineer is on board. As flexible as it is, the Stinger lacks in raw armor and firepower, its acid doing negligible damage to structures.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Stormchild
entries.content:
The Stormchild is an advanced delta-winged jet fighter with canards, specifically equipped to efficiently deal with fast moving targets. With its high-tech lasers and powerful targeting systems, it's theoretically impossible for the fighter to miss its target. Its plentiful missiles benefit from the targeting systems as well, though they cause less damage individually than comparable warheads. Although the Stormchild is one of the fastest fighters in the Allied arsenal, it is rather fragile in the face of anti-aircraft fire. Due to a low radar cross-section, the fighter is invisible on enemy radars, giving the Stormchild the element of surprise.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Stryker IFV
entries.content:
The Stryker Infantry Fighting Vehicle (or the Stryker IFV for short) is the newest development in multipurpose support vehicles. It is an eight-wheeled armored vehicle that comes equipped with standard light anti-armor missiles capable of accurately taking down enemy aircraft with great ease even while on the move. Its great speed, the highest among its peers, allows it to effectively perform hit and run tactics.
But the Stryker's greatest strength lies in its ability to adapt to almost any situation presented to an Allied commander. This vehicle houses a complex weapons system which allows any infantry that enters it to integrate their weapon into the turret of the Stryker. Because of that, the Stryker's weaponry automatically changes depending on what type of infantryman is operating it.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Stun Grid
entries.content:
The Stun Grid is a hidden yet intricate defensive structure used by Foehn. It is a special electric grid that traps any hapless enemy infantry who happens to step on it, stunning them as long as they remain on the grid. Stun Grids can also stun infiltration units.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Suppressor
entries.content:
The Suppressor is a Pacific Front amphibious combat specialist infantry unit type that are capable of converting incoming damage into healing for friendly troops using a compact version of a specialized piece of equipment called the "Negation Field". This device is capable of reverting the destructive nature of every projectile to point, where attacking would simply heal the target - with an opposite result for any repairing or healing tool.instead, making them unusually valuable. They usually float into battle on their specialized V-shaped hoverboards, giving them all-terain and even amphibious qualities.
It is used by Pacific Front.

entries.name: Sweeper
entries.content:
The Sweeper is an x-shaped hovering combat drone used by the Last Bastion, armed with Golden Rocket multi-launchers that can only attack ground targets when deployed. When they are not deployed, they are  hidden from their enemies' sight, making the Sweeper useful for ambushes.
It is used by Last Bastion.

entries.name: Swordfish
entries.content:
The Swordfish is the Foehn Revolt's premier naval unit, a light gunboat serving as the backbone of their fleet. Armed with an upgraded pressurizer lance (stronger than Lancers' version), it can engage large warships effectively. Its air-manipulating engine grants exceptional speed, especially useful in coastal combat. While not as common as Spinblades inland, Swordfishes dominate naval warfare with their firepower and agility. 
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Syncronaut
entries.content:
The Syncronaut is the upgraded version of the Syncronin created when one is infused by a Nanofiber Sync. They are better armored with a new, darker power armor, invisible to enemies' view and uses a different bond breaker that affects buildings around them instead of a single structure, although it has to be used up close.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Syncronin
entries.content:
The Syncronin is a power-armored Foehn infantry specialist that has a peculiar weapon in the form of an atomic-level bond breaker, which when used on enemy structures, makes the cohesion of the materials they're built from considerably weaker. With their lowered resistance to damage, a Foehn commander can largely decrease the time necessary to destroy enemy bases. The effects of Syncronin's bond breaker are accumulative, meaning that if more than one of them targets a building, its material cohesion will weaken even more, further increasing its vulnerability.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Synthesis Vault
entries.content:
Synthesis Vault is a tall tower with several bio-reactors attached to it's top. it is used by Yuri's forces for basic biological research and material processing. His unique infantry treatment drugs are distributed from this building, with both fundamental and advanced types. In addition, the special materials synthesized through this building can also be used to build Tank Bunkers as well as deploy the Ruiner of Epsilon HQ. What's more, the synthetic energy emitted from this structure is conducted through the Tank Bunkers nearby, actively reinforcing their internal structure.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Tank Bunker
entries.content:
Tank Bunkers are structures, which most turreted vehicles can enter to gain additional protection from enemy fire while still being able to retaliate. Though the occupier of a Bunker will become a much more difficult target to destroy for ground forces, aerial attacks will still easily bypass these entrenchments. Tank Bunkers built nearby a Synthesis Vault can get their armor reinforced with supplemental active field coming from the Vault.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Tanya Adams
entries.content:
Tanya Adams is a mysterious and legendary tomboyish U.S. special agent whose true origins are known only to a few now high-ranking officials
A lean, muscular operative with short brown hair, Tanya wears a tank top, camo cargo pants, a utility belt, and combat boots. Her signature weapon is an early miniaturized laser capable of slicing through tanks, ships, and flesh effortlessly. She also carries C4 charges, allowing her to demolish enemy structures instantly. This combination makes her a deadly force in any combat scenario, on land or at sea. As of now, she has a seat on the Foehn Leadership council after leading the allied remnants on their escape to Point Hope from Antarctica.

entries.name: Tarchia
entries.content:
The Tarchia is a hovering bulky and wide self-propelled plasma howitzer that moves slowly but can use Spinblades for speed boosts. It fires long-range plasma blasts, devastating enemy defenses, structures, and units. However, it cannot fire while moving and must recalibrate after repositioning. Ideal for sieges, its anti-grav chassis allows it to traverse any terrain, including water.
It is used by Wings of Coronia.

entries.name: Tech Center
entries.content:
Together with the subfaction-specific technology expansion buildings like the Mercury Network Uplink, the Shield Command and Robot Ops Control Center, the Allied Tech Center unlocks the most potent technologies and weapons the Allies have to offer to a commander.
The Tech Center is a tall glass building with many laboratories and research facilities inside. It also allows the allies to release the Black Widow or its Alpha variant. Additionally, it can upgrade the Arsenal Depot's Cryoshot into the Cryospear, and if an Experimental Warpshop is present on the battlefield, access to Backwarp will be available.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Tech Protector
entries.content: The Tech Protector is a tech defense that gives additional strength to all ground vehicles stationed around this structure, when captured. The Tech Protectors are advanced devices, scattered throughought[sic] the battlefield at key locations, with the capability to reinforce the armor of units in its range, with an active shield, at the cost of some power.

entries.name: Tech turret
entries.content: The Tech Turret is a neutral defensive structure that, when captured, is basically a rotatable 120mm cannon turret which can effectively engage vehicles.

entries.name: Tempest architect
entries.content:
The Tempest Architect the offensive superweapon of the Foehn Revolt. It, as its name suggests, is the pinnacle of the Foehn's wind control technology, as it can unleash a highly destructive singularity of raging wind upon enemy forces. Visually, it resembles a mushroom-like high tech facility protruding from the center of a square-like foundation.
When the Tempest Architect gathers the winds within a vortex, it is capable of unleashing its destructive energy, which will continuously deal heavy damage to a designated area for a short period of time, taking down the sturdiest of buildings, vehicles and even aircraft alike.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Teratorn
entries.content:
The Teratorn is Foehn’s H-shaped, four-tracked anti-aircraft drone, specializing in air targets but defenseless against ground units. It uses "golden rockets"—fast, durable, and highly explosive—requiring a brief lock-on delay to ensure accuracy. Despite this, it can fire while moving, delivering devastating firepower against enemy aircraft. 
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Terminus drugs
entries.content:
A powerful mixture of aerosol steroids, bio-augmentative chemicals, and hormones known as the Terminus Drugs. When either inhaled or directly injected, the terminus chemicals shall immediately and temporarily amplify their user's aggression, physical strength, perception, endurance and pain tolerance.
They are used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Terranova virus
entries.content: A virus created by Epsilon's chief geneticists and virologists, it mutates those that are infected with it into hulking muscular grey-skinned brute mutants. Depending on how the terranova virus interfaces with the genetic makeup of those affected, the intelligence of one such mutant may either become severely diminished, or be retained.

entries.name: Terror drone
entries.content:
Terror Drones are small, agile quadrupedal robots—the Soviets' deadliest infantry-scale unit. Armed with razor-sharp cutters, they shred armor and infantry alike like "a hot knife through butter," excelling as anti-armor saboteurs. Once latched onto a vehicle, only specialized repair units can remove them, often forcing desperate commanders to destroy infected friendlies.
Their robotic nature grants immunity to mind control, radiation, and toxins, making them universal threats. However, they’re vulnerable to small arms and air strikes. Their compact size allows transport concealment, enabling deadly ambushes. A psychological weapon disguised as machinery.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Tesla Coil
entries.content:
Soviet Tesla Coils have always brought hesitation and sometimes even fear to even the most hardened of Allied soldiers. Men reduced to ash in the blink of an eye and tanks ripped apart by powerful discharges of pure electricity makes commanders of all factions wary of this potent base defense. The Tesla Coil has been redesigned to allow Tesla Troopers to lend additional charge to the coil, making its arcs even more powerful, and even allowing it to function without base power.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Tesla Cruiser
entries.content:
The Tesla Cruiser is a fully tracked vehicle mounted with two small, turret-mounted tesla coils. Although they have shorter range and less lethality than their stationary counterpart, the Tesla Cruiser can easily make short work of enemy vehicles and infantry. The Tesla Cruiser's coils can short-circuit tanks as well, temporarily disabling them. This makes the vehicle an ideal tank destroyer, but defenses and buildings will prove too tough for lone Tesla Cruisers to assault directly.
It is used by Russia.

entries.name: Tesla Reactor
entries.content:
Tesla Reactors are generators that produce a regenerative feedback loop of electricity that provides cheap, renewable energy to Soviet bases. An electricity current is created and stored in the large containment orb. When the amount of energy exceeds the containment capacity point, a breakdown occurs with the energy discharging to the base, which generates the vivid display of an energy arc and creates a new energy current.
It is used by all three Soviet subfactions.

entries.name: Tesla trooper
entries.content:
The Tesla Trooper is an important part of every Soviet infantry division, making full use of the advances in tesla technology, and thus maintaining his position as one of the Soviets best anti-tank troopers. The thick insulative armor provides protection from tank treads and dog bites as well, making the Tesla Trooper even more durable. A recent development is the coil charger, which allows troopers to charge a friendly Tesla Coil, allowing the Coil to remain online without grid power and increasing its lethality.
It is used by Latin Confederation and China.

entries.name: The American General
keys: Field commander of the Allied Nations
entries.content:
The american general is the Allies' best field commander during the Third Great War and Mental Omega War. This American officer led Allied resistance against the Soviet Union and later, the Epsilon Army, throughout the conflicts.
Little is known about the commander's life, as the record is classified Top Secret by the Allied Forces, with the exception that he sacrificed his life leading the Paradox Engine in an ultimately futile kamikaze strike against the Mental Omega Device

entries.name: The Last Bastion
entries.content:
The Last Bastion originated as Point Hope, Alaska, where the Foehn Revolt made their final stand against Epsilon’s mind control. After failing to escape via space, they fortified Point Hope—the "second furthest point" from the Mental Omega Device—to resist its psychic influence.
With the Paradox Engine’s wreckage chronoshifted to the site, the Revolt created a time bubble, shielding Point Hope from Epsilon’s control. Inside, they rapidly advanced technology and built a resistance force.
The Last Bastion is the Foehn Revolt's "defensive" miitary branch, focused on fortifying and protecting their current territory and the massive fortress that is current Point Hope. They specalize in: high survivability, advanced long-range area denial and usage of nanotechnology

entries.name: The Soviet General
entries.content:
The unknown Soviet General is an extremely talented Russian general of the Third Great War and later, the Mental Omega War. He served the Soviet Union during both conflicts as a field commander. Little is known of the general's life, as almost all information about him, including his name, is a state secret of the Soviet Union.
Prior to his deployment to the American front, the Soviet General is known as a top graduate in the Soviet Military Academy.
Folowing his daring assault on Moscow to kill Yuri, he succeeded, but not before him and the rest of his forces fell under the global influence of the Mental Omega Device, sending one last warning to his lunar comrades before he became a mind controlled thrall.

entries.name: The spy
entries.content:
The Spy is the Allies' espionage infantry. They can disguise themselves as enemy infantry to infiltrate their buildings. When not wearing a disguise, they're dress in black suits and wear a pair of sunglasses to conceal their identity.
They are used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Third Great War
entries.content: The Third Great War (GWIII or WWIII) erupted in 1982 and ended in 1983 when the Soviet Union, led by Russia and allied with China and the Latin Confederation, invaded the U.S. and Europe, aided by Yuri’s mind-controlling PsiCorps. The Allied Nations (U.S., European Alliance, Pacific Front) resisted but ultimately lost after Soviet nuclear strikes secured dominance over North America and Europe, except the British Isles. Russia also crushed a Chinese/Pacific Front rebellion. Key events included invasions of America and Europe, a failed Allied counter-invasion of Russia, African/Middle Eastern insurgencies, and Chinese civil conflict with PsiCorps interference.

entries.name: Thor Gunship
entries.content:
The Thor Gunship is a colossal aerial warship and the pride of the European Alliance, designed by an independent arms developer linked to Siegfried. Powered by a massive central turbine, it dominates the battlefield with its "Mjölnir" conduction drones—small, chrono-shifted units that summon devastating lightning strikes on laser-marked targets, vaporizing infantry and crippling aircraft before disappearing.
Beyond its firepower, the Thor serves as a mobile command hub, temporarily directing ground forces into defensive maneuvers. Its presence alone boosts Allied morale, symbolizing Europe’s military supremacy. Awe-inspiring yet vulnerable without escort, the Thor is a high-impact asset in large-scale engagements. 
It is used by European Alliance.

entries.name: Tigr APC
entries.content:
The Tigr APC is the Russian counterpart to the standard Halftrack. Although the main armament has not changed much in comparison, the Tigr is much better armored, and thus slower, than the Halftrack. This makes the unit an effective support for the Russian Wolfhounds, and a better defense against heavier air threats. Its lower speed, however, doesn't make the Tigr APC less of an effective transport as it can carry an additional passenger compared to the Halftrack
It is used by Russia.

entries.name: Time Bubble
entries.content: Created by using the powerful Chronosphere within the wreckage of the Paradox Engine, the Foehn Time Bubble is a wide field that protects Point Hope and the surrounding areas from the influence of Epsilon's Mental Omega device by creating a temporal bubble where time flows much differently than in the rest of the world. It's radius is 100 kilometers around Point Hope.

entries.name: Point Hope
entries.content:
Point Hope is protected by the Time Bubble, a special sphere of temporal energy emanating from the hastily repaired chronosphere within the Paradox Engine's wreckage that envelops the entire location thanks to the repaired and reconfigured chronosphere located within the wreckage of the Paradox Engine located in the center of Point Hope. Said field blocks off and protects those inside Point Hope and it's closest surrounding areas from falling under the psychic influence of the Mental Omega Device.
Time flows very differently within the Time Bubble and it is almost impossible to enter or exit it without either special equipment or vehicles which are protected from both Mind Control and the Time Bubble's chrono barriers.

entries.name: Trident Battleship
entries.content:
The Trident-class Battleship is a modernized Allied capital ship, originally kept in service post-war due to their large numbers. Upgraded with larger-caliber guns, advanced radars, and electronics, they excel in long-range naval bombardment, specializing in anti-vehicle strikes. During the Soviet resurgence, they defended the British Isles alongside the Gladius Defense Network, stalling enemy advances. Proving their enduring value, Tridents remain a symbol of the Allies' naval supremacy, combining firepower and reliability in prolonged conflicts.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Tsurugi powersuit
entries.content:
The Tsurugi Powersuit is the Pacific Front's equivalent to the American Stryker and the European Archon, but with higher passenger survivability rate and immunity to depilot, toxin and radiation. It is a four meter-tall mech with two backwards bent legs, which is capable of carrying only a single passenger within it's cockpit. Just like the american It's weaponry automatically  changes depending on what type of infantryman is operating it.
It is used by Pacific Front.

entries.name: Tu-114
entries.content:
The Tupolev Tu-114 Rossiya is a large turboprop-powered long-range airliner designed by the Tupolev design bureau and primarily used by all three factions of the Epsilon army. Due to its swept wing and powerplant design, the Tu-114 was able to travel at speeds typical of modern jetliners, 880 km/h (550 mph).
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Turmoil grid
entries.content:
The Turmoil Grid is a special ground-layed cybernetic grid does not trap soldiers, but instead applies a quick confusion shock to any unit or infantry that moves through it. The affected unit will continue to have the confusion effect reapplied until it leaves the Turmoil Grid's area or the base goes low on power. Just like the Stun Grid, the Turmoil Grid will automatically react to spies and other disguised infantry
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Typhoon
entries.content:
The main warship of various Soviet naval forces, Typhoons are submarines capable of moving quickly through the sea, ambushing any enemies with a salvo of torpedoes, quickly sinking them, and returning to the depths within seconds. Though they are one of the worlds most dangerous ship killers, they cannot attack land targets and have difficulty maneuvering due to their length.
Two different sets of torpedoes are loaded onto Typhoons: Type-O, a standard precise and effective type of torpedo, and Type-T, which has a tesla-tipped highly explosive warhead, capable of travelling at larger distances and greater speeds at the cost of its accuracy and reload time.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Tyrant tank
entries.content:
The Tyrant, Scorpion Cell's heavy tank, combines underground mobility (thanks to a front grinder and reinforced armor) with devastating toxin/acid bombardments from its fixed turret. Designed for shock assaults, it trades armor quality for speed, relying on numerical superiority rather than brute strength. While weaker than Allied/Soviet heavies, its ability to burrow and swarm makes it a relentless conqueror in Rashidi's campaigns—striking fast, poisoning foes, and vanishing before counterattacks land. 
It is used by Scorpion Cell.

entries.name: Ultra Dome
entries.content:
The Ultra Dome is a unique Euro Alliance device, which has been designed to synchronize all the defenses in its vicinity and make it easier for their systems to exchange information regarding the enemy positions - past, present and in the predicted future. Enhanced with the Ultra Dome, the defensive structures around it will deal bigger damage than usual. Due to its complicated internal composition and technology, Ultra Domes are scarce in numbers - a european army can only build one of them on the battlefield.
It is used by European Alliance.

entries.name: United States of America
entries.content: The U.S. joined WW2 after Soviet nuclear threats, later occupying Russia before Yuri forced their withdrawal. In 1982's Third Great War, Soviet forces invaded America, finally succeeding after the assassination of President Dugan and establishing an network of Psychic Beacons. The U.S. collapsed into resistance cells as the USSR took over the country. Yuri's 1984 Epsilon coup then broke Soviet control and plunged the country into further anarchy. US remnants like Tanya and Carville regrouped with other alied forces in Alaska. After the Paradox Engine's failure to destroy the Mental Omega Device, allied survivors joined the Foehn Revolt. Today, only Point Hope remains free from Epsilon's global psychic domination.

entries.name: Uragan
entries.content:
Uragan is a young sub-routine of the long-established VOLKNET A.I. interned within a tall, white-painted robot body with three vertical pairs of eye-sensors within it's artificial head, it runs most of the Last Bastion's command, intelligence and security systems, and has actually been created during the very last phase of the Bastion's base operations.
As the Bastion lacks dedicated artillery, Uragan serves as a mobile siege weapon—slow but heavily armored, capable of enduring AA fire while delivering devastating plasma strikes. Its triple-eye sensors and command role make it a unique hybrid of firepower and tactical intelligence, crucial for destroying enemy strongholds.

entries.name: Virus
entries.content:
Beautiful yet lethal, the Virus snipers are genetic offshoots of a super-soldier program, perfected for assassination. Originally Rashidi's elite guard, they fire bio-engineered darts carrying a horrific pathogen. Victims develop necrotic sores before rupturing into toxic gas clouds, infecting nearby troops—though the contagion quickly dissipates.
Enhanced in Yuri's labs, Viruses are immune to toxins and even strengthened by them. Their precision marksmanship makes them deadly against infantry, picking off targets with ease. More than snipers, they're biological weapons—turning each kill into a spreading nightmare for enemy forces.
They are used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: VOLKNET
entries.content:
VOLKNET, an advanced AI created by Yunru with Chinese and Kanegawa Industries' expertise, debuted during the Kashmir conflict. Operating from a Mainframe, it was destroyed when Yunru nuked invading Soviets with a MIDAS.
Mysteriously reactivated, VOLKNET then guided Yunru's escape to Mangla Dam Lake, evading pursuers. It later commanded key Revolt missions—securing the Ironwing in Kazakhstan, aiding Kanegawa allies, assaulting an Epsilon spaceport, freeing Point Hope, and establishing the time bubble defense.
As of now he serves as both the AI infrastructure of Foehn settlements and as the supreme general of their armies.

entries.name: Volkov
entries.content:
Volkov, the USSR's resurrected cybernetic commando, wielded an experimental tesla rifle that chains lightning between enemies—too deadly for normal humans. Enhanced with Overcharge support and immune to radiation/toxins, his only weaknesses are EMP and magnetic weapons. He fought alongside his loyal cybernetic dog Chitzkoi.
Once the Soviets' top operative, Volkov was destroyed in the Second Great War after going berserk from Allied hacking attempts. Though engineers assure his new tamper-proof systems and encrypted codes prevent repeats, some officials distrust his reactivation. Now reborn as Russia's ultimate warrior, he remains an unstoppable symbol of Soviet power.
After being personally mind controlled by Yuri, he was finally destroyed by his own friendly forces again during the soviet assault on Yuri-controlled Moscow.

entries.name: Voyager
entries.content:
The Voyager Transport is the Allies' amphibious hovercraft transport vehicle. The Voyager is equipped with dual missile pods, allowing it to defend itself from attacks from both ground and air forces.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Vulture
entries.content:
The Vulture is a uniquely versatile latin confederate helicopter, combining a fast attack chopper to chase and mow down infantry and a light Kirov-like bomber unit when ordered to deploy. With the special napalm bomb, the chopper is capable of setting the ground below on fire, making it an effective barrier for enemy infantry and light vehicles. While its set of machine guns is quite a powerful weapon on its own, due to its thin armor, Vulture should be protected from even the feeblest of anti-aircraft forces.
It is used by European Confederation.

entries.name: War miner
entries.content:
The war miner is a soviet tracked remote controlled miner vehicle armed with a machinegun turret for self-defense. it is used by all three factions of the Soviet Union and has double the ore-carrying capacity of your average miner.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: War Rig
entries.content:
At first glance, this building is not much different from Epsilon's regular Ore Refinery, but the fact is that the War Rig, known as "the Epsilon's Swiss Army Knife", serves more than just providing an ore unloading point. It can provide repair services for the surrounding vehicles, just like the Soviet Repair Crane. The building's top is equipped with an Amnesia Ray, same as the Ruiner's, to deprive the attack capability of enemy soldiers who approach it. Moreover, the same active energy emitters as those in the Synthesis Vault are contained inside the Rig, to reinforce any nearby Tank Bunkers.
It is used by all three Epsilon Subfactions.

entries.name: Warhawk
entries.content:
The Warhawk is a lightly armored american attack helicopter used by the Americans for close air support. It's outfitted with a heavy laser cannon on it's nose turret to light infantry ablaze and slice through tank armor, as well as the 'Uranus' missile pods, which can make short work of enemy ground targets. The Warhawk does not carry any anti-aircraft weaponry and relies on its quick speed to evade potential threats. This is mostly due to the United States' efforts to design effective methods of supporting their flying troops the Warhawk can heal air infantry like Rocketeer nearby as it carries special first aid equipment for them all the time.
It is used by the United States of America.

entries.name: Warpnode
entries.content:
Warpnode is a derivative product of the Experimental Warpshop, being designed along with the Chronolift support. When a Warpnode appears somewhere on the battlefield, it's operator can move the building they want next to it through the Chronolift. However, due to the unstable and risky nature of the process, only up to three Warpnodes can be operated at the same time.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Watercat
entries.content:
The hovering Watercat Transport is Foehn's amphibious transport vehicle with four pairs of jet engines at it's back. Respectably fast and durable, they are useful for carrying land vehicles between islands.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Weather Controller
entries.content:
The Weather Controller is one of the Allies' most powerful weapons. it is an exotic-looking building that has four dyametrically opposed metallic weather control spheres connected to a bigger sphere that stands on a platform, it has the unique ability to manipulate weather patterns in order to form storm clouds over any location on the battlefield. These storm clouds will unleash powerful bolts of lightning, disintegrating a large area into ash. Be aware that the lightning strikes are completely random, so hitting the exact targeted spot is not guaranteed.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Widow Alpha
entries.content:
The Black Widow Alpha is a superior version of the Black Widow used by the United States. Not fully satisfied with the standard Black Widow, the US spent additional resources on the Black Widow Alpha, which functions identically but is slightly tougher and lasts longer.
It is used by all three Allied Subfactions.

entries.name: Windtrap
entries.content:
The advanced technologies of the Revolt require lots of energy to be produced and maintained, so there was a need to design a power plant which would fullfil most of the requirements on the go as soon as a new outpost is built. This is where Foehn's high-level understanding of the forces of nature, revolving around the creation and flow of winds comes in handy - a power plant that traps the wind and, by using complicated methods, is able to generate power with its constant movement. Windtraps are larger and more expensive than the other power plants, but produce more energy than an average one. Visually, it resembles a highly technological cone-shaped structure.
It is used by all three Foehn Subfactions.

entries.name: Wolfhound
entries.content:
The Wolfhound is a powerful russian attack helicopter capable of tackling the toughest of adversaries, whether on the ground or in the air. Once the Wolfhound has locked onto its quarry, the flurry of missiles or its high-powered machine gun will be sure to rip its target apart. Though powerful, Wolfhounds are sluggish and will fall victim to enemy anti-aircraft fire if caught up in it.
It is used by all three Russian Subfactions.

entries.name: Wonder drugs
entries.content: Wonder drugs are essentially Regen drugs, but made more efficient via a more complex chemical process. The difference between them and regular regen drugs is that wonder drugs last much longer.

entries.name: Xiurong Wu
entries.content:
A high ranking Chinese Communist Party member and chinese field commander. He failed in invading Primorsky Krai against Soviet forces. After the Third Great War, he learned that Yunru, a key military scientist, was captured by Yuri when transferring a psychic to him—a move against Yuri’s broken pact with China. Wu deployed his elite Feng Squad to rescue her in Afghanistan.
Later, during the Mental Omega War, Wu defended Shanghai’s Military Headquarters against a russian invasion. Despite his tactical insight, he was defeated and captured for interrogation, before being executed.

entries.name: Yunru
entries.content:
Yunru was once brilliant scientist blackmailed into developing weapons for the Chinese army. After she was captured by PsiCorps in Afghanistan, and afterwards rescured by a chinese strikeforce, she learned about Yuri's sinister plan and the sheer threat against the world he posed. However, her superiors dismissed her concern, forcing her to start secretly planning and organizing what would become the Foehn Revolt. After the destruction of the Kashmiri base where she was held captive, she and her fellow Foehn rebels managed to escape to Japan where they linked up with their Pacific Front sympathizers, rescued her contact Rashidi and conquered the former Epsilon Base in Point Hope, establishing the Foehn stronghold upon it's ruins. As of now, she is the head of the Foehn Revolt's RND and has a leading seat on the Revolt's leadership Council, bearing the title of the Architect.
She is 5.3'', wears a labcoat over a white blouse covered in black dots and a dark cyan-colored skirt, while her eyes are usually conceale by a pair of engineering goggles. Her hair is pink and she has three braids on each side of her head, earning her the derogative nickname of "Axolotl".

entries.name: Yuri
entries.content: Yuri was once the leader of the entire Epsilon faction. Yuri emerged from Stalin's psychic programs, developing mind control tech before WWIII. During the war, he manipulated both sides - forcing Allied withdrawal from Russia and poisoning hero Boris. When exposed, he fled with stolen rocket tech to form the Epsilon Army. After two years preparing lunar/Antarctic bases, Epsilon attacked in 1984, killing Romanov and conquering Russia. Though countered by Allied time-freezing tech, Yuri deployed psychic supersoldier Libra. His final Moscow stand used mind-controlled Volkov against Soviet forces. Yuri's death became the perfect sacrifice - Distracting the soviet force in order to allow the relatively uninterrupted triggering the Mental Omega Device and global psychic enslavement.

entries.name: Zephyr Artillery
entries.content:
The four-tracked Zephyr Artillery is a self-propelled anti-tank artillery utilized by the Pacific Front to combat large armor columns from a safe distance. If a special zephyrobot was deployed within a specific area, then it would allow the Zephyrs to target anything within the area of the drone by using it as a targetting beacon. Though a formidable foe at long range, the Zephyr is lightly armored in order to incorporate the needed targeting mechanisms. The minimum range of the weapon is another one of its weak points, so it shouldn't be sent unguarded into the field.
It is used by all Pacific Front.

entries.name: Zorbfloater
entries.content:
The Zorbfloater is the upgraded version of the Zorbtrotter created when infused by a Nanofiber Sync. While mostly unchanged except for this new, darker bodyarmor, they trade off the ability to create vacuum spheres for increased resistance to enemy fire and rapid health regeneration.
What makes the Zorbfloater truly amazing, though, is that their upgraded wind manipulation apparatus are strong enough to lift most, if not all, vehicles into the air and draw it towards them!
They are used by Wings of Coronia.

entries.name: Zorbtrotters
entries.content:
The Zorbtrotters, elite Foehn soldiers from Coronia, wield air manipulation so advanced its origins are debated—whether through miniaturized tech or innate psychic-like abilities, possibly linked to Epsilon defectors.
Their deadliest weapon is oxygen denial, creating airless spheres that suffocate infantry. Additionally, they harness wind control to enhance mobility, using Spinblades for speed boosts and even walking on wate, while surrounding themseves with a thick wind bubble that offers them protection.
Clad in simple armor, their lethality lies in mastery over wind manipulation, making them unstoppable against breath-dependent foes while maintaining superior battlefield agility.
They are used by Wings of Coronia.

entries.name: Zubr transport
entries.content:
The Zubr is the Soviet amphibious transport, capable of ferrying large amounts of forces over water. These massive hovercrafts can transport both infantry and armor to any location and keep it out of harm's way. Though Zubr Transports are armed and can swat away light or half-hearted attacks from the sky, they should not be put in harm's way to prevent severe and unnecessary losses as they are not as hardy as the animal they are named after.
It is used by all three Soviet Subfactions.

entries.name: Tank killer
entries.content: The flame tower is a defensive structure used by the Latin Confederation. It is essentially a remote-controlled tall turret armed with a flamethrower, with two fuel tanks at the top.

entries.name: Hydra cannon
entries.content: Despite the name, it is not a cannon, but is essentialy a light tracked anti-personnel vehicle used by Russia. It's frontal turret is equipped with two high caliber gatling guns, while the back of it's hull has an ATGM launcher.

entries.name: Repair drone
entries.content: During the Second Great War, the Soviets used service depots for vehicle repairs, unlike the Allies who later deployed field mechanics. Lacking dedicated repair personnel, the Soviets developed hover-capable repair drones before the Third Great War. Deployed via jet, these drones could repair ground and naval units but were lightly armored and vulnerable without protection. They are used by all three soviet subfactions.

entries.name: Ruiner
entries.content:
Epsilon HQ's Ruiner is a UFO-like unit equipped with the Amnesia Ray, a weapon that chemically induces amnesia in enemy infantry, preventing them from using their weapons. The ray manipulates human senses through advanced genetic research. Affected troops act as catalysts, spreading the effect to nearby units and disabling entire squads. To ensure effectiveness in mixed combat, Yuri modified his Brutes to be immune to the Amnesia Ray, allowing the Ruiner to function as a powerful support unit without harming his own forces. This highlights Yuri’s strategic brilliance and mastery of mind control technologies.
It is used by Epsilon HQ.

entries.name: Future Tank X-0
entries.content: The Chrono Prison is a secret Allied vehicle that uses advanced chrono technology to teleport enemy units to an unknown location. There, the drivers are either brainwashed or replaced, and the units return loyal to the Allies. Some believe it involves mind control in an alternate dimension, but its true nature remains hidden to all but a few.

entries.name: Future Tank X-1
entries.content:
The Future Tank X-1, a larger, stronger successor to the X-0, was developed after the Okawa Falls disaster but never reached mass production due to war losses and foreign invasions. Kanegawa Industries ceased the project, destroying its data. However, some units survived and were later upgraded in secret. The Alpha version features advanced tech and dual weapon modes: laser and grenade combo, or a powerful particle collider cannon.
It is in use with the Pacific Front and the Foehn Revolt

entries.name: Medic bunker
entries.content: The medic bunker is a small fortified structure typically in use with armies of all countries within the Soviet Union. Just like the name says, it essentially serves as a field hospital for their wounded infantry.

entries.name: 1986 Earth
entries.content: After the Mental Omega war, nearly all humanity was psychically enslaved via the Mental Omega Device. Its use caused massive South Pole melting, flooding much of the world. Ruins of soviet nuclear tech spread radiation across battlefields. Cities lie in ruins, while remaining bases and settlements are being reshaped into vast hive-like metropolises under Epsilon hivemind control.

entries.name: Lionheart
entries.content:
The Lionheart is an exceptional highly futuristic hypersonic bomber in the Allied air force as, instead of missiles, it relies on simple, but effective fuel bombs with a heavily modified electromagnetic pulse warhead, that was seized from one of the Chinese-controlled labs during the war. Whatever the Lionheart does not kill, it will at least immobilize for a good while. This combination makes the Lionheart Bomber a very effective armor killer, which will help you in quickly blowing the enemy armored battalions and infantry squads to smithereens.
It is used by the Allied Remnants.
